-># **Hermetic Philosophy**<-
<note>original Latin: "PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA"</note>

*The frontispiece displays a circular symbolic emblem set against a rectangular background.*

*In the center of the image, a pelican is depicted in her "piety" <term>Pelican in her piety: A powerful symbol in both alchemy and Christian iconography, representing a mother bird feeding her young with her own blood; in this context, it signifies the "Great Work" of self-sacrifice and the revitalization of matter.</term>. She stands upon a cubic altar, which represents the stability of the physical world. On the front face of this cube are four red roses arranged in a square pattern, a signature of Rosicrucian thought.* <note>The rose and the cross/cube symbolize the union of the divine spirit with the material body.</note>

*The scene is bathed in golden light radiating from a sun at the top of the composition. Curving over the sun is an Ouroboros <term>Ouroboros: An ancient symbol of a serpent consuming its own tail, representing the eternal cycle of life, death, and rebirth, and the idea that "All is One."</term>. The entire central oval is framed by a border of green, representing growth and the natural world.*

# Treatise and Wander-
## ing of the Highly Celebrated Lord Sa-
## lomon Trismosin, together with three
### powerful Tinctures.

<image-desc>A large decorative historiated woodcut initial 'D' featuring intricate strapwork and foliage patterns.</image-desc>
When I was a young journeyman, I came to a miner named Flocker, who was also an alchemical artist; however, he kept all his affairs hidden, and I could obtain nothing from him. <margin>lead</margin> He had a piece of common Saturn <note>original: "♄"; the alchemical symbol for lead, named for the slow-moving planet.</note> and a special sulfur or brimstone with it, and he fixed <note>original: "siegierte," from the Latin *sigillare*, meaning to seal or fix a volatile substance into a solid state.</note> the Saturn for so long until it became firm and fluid, and afterwards like wax. To prepare this Saturn, he took 20 *Loth* <term>Loth: A traditional German unit of weight, approximately 1/2 ounce or 15 grams.</term> and 1 mark of fine silver which contained no gold, let both melt together for half a day, and then he separated this silver through a casting so that it became half gold. My heart was greatly pained that I was not to possess this art, and I thought to ask him about it, but it was denied me. Not long after, he was buried in a mine <note>original: "verfallt er in einem Berg"; likely referring to a fatal mining accident or cave-in.</note>, and no one could find anything of his art. Because I had seen this truth myself with this miner, I set out in the year 1473 and traveled back and forth; wherever I heard of an artist, I made an effort to reach him, and spent a year and a half in this wandering. I learned all sorts of arts from alchemy which did not amount to much, though I saw the truth in certain particulars <term>Particulars: Minor alchemical operations (particularia) that could change the appearance or properties of metals but did not involve the "Universal" Philosophers' Stone.</term> and spent 200 florins, yet I did not think of giving up.

I thought and was diligent to raise travel-funds among my friends, and took my journey with a stranger

# Treatise and Wandering

I traveled toward Laibach <note>modern Ljubljana, Slovenia</note>, from there toward Milan, and came into a monastery where I served as a student-assistant <note>original: "famulierte," referring to a student who performs domestic duties in exchange for tuition.</note> and attended fine lectures for almost a year. Afterward, I traveled everywhere back and forth in Italy <note>original: "Welschlandt," a historical German term for Latin-speaking or Romance-language lands.</note> and came to an Italian merchant and a Jew who could speak German. These men made English tin <term>Tin: A base metal often used by "sophisticators" to mimic silver due to its bright, white appearance.</term> look like the best fine silver; they sold much of it. I offered to serve them if it pleased them: the Jew persuaded the merchant to take me on as a servant, and I had to tend the fire when they performed their "art" with the tin. I was industrious, and it pleased them well; therefore, they kept nothing hidden from me, and so I also learned the art, which involved poisonous substances. I stayed with them for fourteen weeks.

Afterward, I traveled with the Jew to Venice. He sold about forty pounds <note>original: "x x x x. pfundt"</note> of the silver to a Turkish merchant. While he was bargaining with the merchant, I took six *Loth* <term>Loth: A traditional German unit of weight; 6 Loth is roughly 3 ounces or 90 grams.</term> of the silver and went to a goldsmith who had two journeymen. One of them knew Latin <note>original: "Latinisch"</note>, and I requested that he test the silver for me. There, he directed me across St. Mark’s Square to an assayer <term>Assayer: A "Probierer," an official official skilled in testing the purity of precious metals.</term> who was very noble and rich. He had three German journeymen assayers who quickly put the metal to the test with very sharp substances <note>likely strong acids or corrosive salts used in mineral analysis</note>, and afterward refined it upon the cupel <term>Cupel: A small, porous bowl (the "Test") used in assaying; base metals are absorbed into the bowl or oxidized, leaving only pure silver or gold.</term>. But it did not stand; it failed the test entirely and all flew away in the fire. I was addressed harshly and asked where I had obtained the silver. I declared that I had brought it to be tested precisely so I could see if it would hold up as good silver.

When I saw the fraud, I no longer returned to the Jew and cared nothing more for this "art." I thought I might eventually fall into misfortune because of the Jew and the false silver. Afterward, I came to a school there in Venice and begged that I might have food twice a day. There, the Rector <note>original: "Rector," the head of the school.</note> had me directed to a hospital <note>original: "Spital"; in the 15th century, these were charitable guesthouses for pilgrims and travelers as much as for the sick.</note> where there were other Germans, and they gave fine food there; it had been endowed for all sorts of nations and foreigners. The next day I went to St. Mark’s Square, and a journeyman assayer from the place where I had previously had the silver tested came up to me; he addressed me, asking if I [had] any more...

[The assayer asked if I] had more: I said no, but I did possess the art of how the silver was made, and I would gladly share it with him. This pleased the assayer well, and he asked me if I could also perform laboratory work <term>Laborieren: The practical, physical work of chemistry and alchemy, such as distilling, melting, and refining in a laboratory.</term>. I said yes, reasonably well. Then he said, if I wished, there was a *Gentiluomo* <note>original: "Centilon," likely a German corruption of the Italian "gentiluomo," meaning a nobleman or gentleman.</note> here who commissioned much laboratory work and had long wanted a German lab assistant. This suited me, and he led me straight to the master's head lab assistant, who was a German named Hans Tauler. He was overjoyed and took me on immediately, giving me two crowns every week plus my meals. Then he led me about six Italian miles from Venice to a large house belonging to the same gentleman, which he called Pontilon <note>Possibly a corruption of "Padiglione" (pavilion) or a specific estate name near Venice.</note>. 

In all my life, I have never seen such laboratory work on all kinds of **particular tinctures** <term>Particular: In alchemy, a "particular" is a process that transmutes only specific base metals into gold or silver, whereas a "universal" work transforms all substances.</term> and on medicines as in this place. Everything one could imagine was kept in stock there, and each lab assistant (there were nine of them) had his own chamber, and they all shared their own cook. Then the head lab assistant gave me a task to work on, which had been sent to the nobleman four days earlier; it was a **coagulation of Mercury** <note>original: "coagulatio Mercurij"; the process of stabilizing or "fixing" liquid mercury into a solid state.</note>. The head assistant mixed all the powders for me so that I would not recognize them, and I had to complete the labor on that piece, which was finished or concluded in two days. 

I was industrious, and this **particular** <gloss>partial transmutation</gloss> succeeded well for me. When the coagulated mass was refined at nine *Loth* <term>Loth: A traditional German unit of weight; nine Loth is roughly 4.5 ounces or 145 grams.</term>, three *Loth* of the best gold came out. This was my first work and my good fortune. The head assistant immediately reported this to the nobleman, who came out to see me unexpectedly. He spoke to me in Latin and called me **Fortunatus** <note>Latin: "The Lucky One" or "The Blessed One."</note>. He was not perfect in Latin and tapped me on the shoulder; I did not understand him well, as he spoke everything corruptly <note>The author implies the nobleman's Latin was grammatically broken or heavily accented.</note>. He presented me with 20 crowns. 

Then I was first bound, by my body and life, in place of an oath, that I would tell no man of the art. In short, it all had to be kept secret, and that was only right. And I say that if someone—as I have seen myself—boasts of this art and has already struck upon the truth, then the eternal justice of GOD will not allow such art to proceed any further for him. Therefore, hold your tongue, even if you possess the highest **tincture**; give from it to the poor.

### Treatise and Travels

I saw that I could observe all kinds of arts with this Gentleman <note>original: "Centilon," a corruption of the Italian *gentiluomo*.</note>, especially as the head lab assistant was very loyal to me. He placed all sorts of arts into my hands and informed me that his generous master spent thirty thousand crowns a year on such arts. He paid cash for every kind of book brought to him in all sorts of languages and showed great honor to those who brought them. I saw this truly with my own eyes: a man named Sarlamethon brought a **tincture** <term>Tincture: An alchemical substance—often a powder or liquid—capable of transmuting base metals into gold or silver.</term> written in the Greek language from foreign lands, for which he was paid 6,000 crowns in cash. The Gentleman immediately had this translated into German and placed it in my hands; I worked through it in fifteen weeks.

<margin>Copper, lead, silver</margin>
With this, I transmuted three metals—Venus (copper) ♀, Jupiter (tin) ♃, and the Moon (silver) ☾ <note>While the margin mentions lead, the symbols in the text represent copper, tin, and silver.</note>—in great quantities, all into the finest gold. And all of this was kept hidden from others.

The Gentleman became so magnificent and powerful—and as they "marry the sea" <note>The *Sposalizio del Mare* (Marriage of the Sea), a major Venetian ceremony where the Doge threw a golden ring into the Adriatic to symbolize Venice's dominion over the waters.</note> every year, leading the entire choir out onto the water to throw a golden ring set with precious stones into the sea—this Gentleman also appeared with his own ships in great splendor. Then a storm arose upon the sea, drowning many great lords; thus this great Gentleman also went to the bottom. Consequently, his noble family ceased all laboratory work, and all the lab assistants were paid in full and dismissed, though the head lab assistant was retained.

So I traveled from Venice to an even better place, where I was entrusted with Kabbalistic and magical books in the Egyptian language. These I had translated into the Greek language, and from that into Latin. There I found and seized the entire "Treasure of the Egyptians." I also saw there what the **subject** <term>Subiectum: Also known as the *Subjectum Physicum*, this refers to the primary base matter or "starting material" required to begin the alchemical Great Work.</term> was, and that the greatest pagan kings had used such tinctures and worked them themselves—namely King Xophar, King Sunsfor, King Xogar, King Xopholat, King Iulaton, King Xoman, and others. All of these possessed a great treasure of the tincture. And it is a thing of wonder that the Eternal Deity revealed such things to the pagans.

# This Book is called Trismosin, wherein are found three powerful Tinctures and more pieces, as follow.

## Thus writes Salomon Trismosin concerning the Red Lion.

<image-desc>Large decorative drop cap initial 'V' containing a stylized bird and foliate patterns.</image-desc> Many great secrets appear in all things in Nature, which the highest God Himself has ordained, so that even the children of men <note>A poetic term for humanity.</note> marvel at them when such things are revealed to them. Great treasures lie within the earthen mountains, from which mankind must sustain and support themselves in this world. For without the earth, man cannot live, as it is from the earth that food and drink come; yet we humans are not worthy of these gifts which the merciful God sends us. Everything is misused through ingratitude toward Almighty God; for this reason, He does not allow many treasures to be revealed. Thus, many Arts remain hidden in this world because of our ingratitude; yet more is revealed to pious people than they might expect, as I have often seen that a poor man has many times come upon something great of gold and silver.

Now the **Red Lion** <term>Red Lion: An alchemical symbol for the "Philosopher's Tincture" or the "Philosopher's Stone" in its most potent, fermented state, capable of transforming base metals.</term> is the greatest treasure in this world, with which the children of men—for whom it is intended—can perform great wonders, so that they may obtain health and wealth.

Firstly, this **Leo** <note>original: "Leo", Latin for Lion.</note> is an inexpressible tinctural being, such that it **tinges** <note>from "thingiert," meaning to color or transform the internal nature of a metal.</note> many thousands of parts in its **augmentation** <term>Augmentation: The process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine.</term>; understand this to include the imperfect metals <term>☿</term> <note>Mercury/Quicksilver</note>, Tin, Lead, **Luna** <note>Silver</note>, and others, at which I myself was terrified <note>In this context, "terrified" implies being struck with awe or holy dread at the power of the transformation.</note>.

Whoever now wishes to work with it must be able to separate the Gold into the highest **spirituality** <note>original: "Geistlichkeit." In alchemy, this refers to the process of volatilizing a solid substance into a "spirit" or essence.</note>; then he will experience greater things than I can write. He must be a swift artist who understands well the **Tinctures** with their **dissolutions**, and also the **governance of the fire**; otherwise, nothing can be accomplished.

# Now follows the Tincture of the Black Eagle, a great secret.

## The Black Eagle.

Take two pounds of raw <term>STEMO</term> <note>original: "STEMO"; a variation of *Stibium*, the alchemical name for Antimony.</note>, which the Philosophers call the **Black Eagle**, the very best you can obtain. From this, make a beautiful red glass, as laboratory workers are accustomed to doing. Take two pounds of this, grind it very fine for four hours on a painter’s stone or a grinding stone, and grind into it eight <term>Loth</term> <note>A historical German unit of weight; 8 Loth is approximately 4 ounces or 125 grams.</note> of well-purified <term>Salmiar</term> <note>original: "Salmiar"; Sal ammoniac (ammonium chloride), frequently used in alchemy as a flux or to create volatile salts.</note>. Put it all into a vial and place it in steaming <term>horse manure</term> <note>original: "Roßmist"; manure was used in alchemy as a source of gentle, consistent heat (fermentation heat) for long-term digestion.</note> for ten days and nights; thus the matter will resolve itself. Let it coagulate gently in a mild heat. Afterward, take the matter out of the glass, grind it small, put it back into a vial, and pour the following vinegar over it. Let it stand for three days and nights. Then pour the vinegar off into another glass or vessel; pour more fresh vinegar onto it and let it extract for three days and nights. Do this with fresh vinegar until it extracts nothing more.

Now take all the extracted vinegar into one glass and evaporate it in ashes until dry; thus the <term>Flowers of Antimony</term> <note>original: "Flores Antimonij"; the powdery sublimate formed when antimony is heated.</note> of the **Black Eagle** will remain at the bottom of the glass. Set it to putrefy with mild heat in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ"; literally "the bath of Mary," a double-boiler used to maintain a steady, gentle temperature.</note> for three days and nights. Then distill it into a receiving glass; distill it slowly at first, then gradually stronger. Thus the burning **Spirit of Sal Ammoniac** rises, and afterward comes a blood-

# Here follows the hellish burning spirit of Sal ammoniac.

Take one pound of genuine <term>Sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "Salmiar"; ammonium chloride, a salt used by alchemists to help "volatize" or carry other substances into a vaporous state.</note> and one and a half pounds of common melted salt. Whatever rises up in a subtle form, take it off and grind it again with an equal weight of common salt. Let it sublimate again. Do this until the Sal ammoniac reveals itself as an **incorporeal spirit**. Grind this spirit and collect it on a smooth stone; put it into a glass and sprinkle it with brandy. Seal the glass well at the top and place it in a <term>Bain-marie</term> <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ"; a gentle water bath used for heating substances evenly.</note> until the spirit <term>dissolves</term> <note>original: "soluiert."</note>. Strain off whatever has not turned to water and <term>putrefy</term> <note>In alchemy, "putrification" is a period of slow heating or digestion intended to break down the structure of a substance.</note> it again. Do this until everything turns to water. When everything is dissolved, put the water into a tall retort glass and distill it in a Bain-marie until half remains. Pour the water back in and draw it off once more; then heat it strongly until everything passes over the <term>helm</term> <note>The "helm" or alembic is the top part of the distilling apparatus where vapors condense.</note>. Then <term>rectify</term> <note>To "rectify" is to repeat the distillation process to achieve the highest possible purity.</note> it until no more <term>dregs</term> <note>original: "feces"; the solid residue left after distillation.</note> remain, and thus the **hellish burning water** is prepared.

## The water for dissolution is as follows.

**Take** one and a half pounds of a strong Austrian brandy; put it into a receiver glass and place it upon an earthen crucible. Add common salt, saltpeter, and calcined white tartar—6 **Loth**<note>A historical German unit of weight; 1 Loth is approximately 15–16 grams or half an ounce.</note> of each—with one pound of brick dust [Ziegelmehl] driven strongly therein, so that the salt-spirits settle well within. Then take the whole water and rectify it through the **helm**<note>The "helm" or alembic head is the top part of a still where vapors condense.</note> from a separate glass; thus the water is ready.

## Two secret pieces in the spiritualization of Gold and Silver, which rise together over the helm.

**In** a **cucurbit** glass<note>A gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation.</note> put 4 Loth of filed **Gold**<note>original: "Golt" / alchemical Sol</note> and 4 Loth of sal ammoniac [Salmiar]. Take <unclear>9</unclear> Loth of fine **Silver**<note>original: "Silber" / alchemical Luna</note> and dissolve it in 17 Loth of **Aqua fortis**<note>original: "Aqua fort"; Latin for "strong water," known today as nitric acid.</note>. Distill this off from the Gold and sal ammoniac, then pour fresh Aqua fortis onto it and draw the water off again until it reaches clarity. Do this with fresh water for the third time; thus the Gold and Silver will rise together over the helm of the crucible and have partly become spiritualized <note>To "spiritualize" a metal meant to convert it from a solid "body" into a vaporous or volatile "spirit."</note>.

Now let the metals in the receiver glass rise gently; let them sit for several days. Wash these with clean warm waters once you have drawn the Aqua fortis off from them. After they are made dry, grind the **calx**<note>A fine powder produced by chemical treatment or intense heat.</note> very small and put it into a glass crucible. Set it in warm ashes for 14 days and turn the glass around often. Afterward, take it out, grind it small, and put it back in the glass in these ashes; let it stand for another 14 days with the fire, and so it will become entirely **fixed**<note>A "fixed" substance is one that has been stabilized so that it no longer evaporates or changes when exposed to high heat.</note>. Then take the third part and reduce it with a **flux**<note>A substance added to help the metal melt and flow.</note> into the best gold.

Now you should have a spiritual silver that has risen over the helm; add just as much again to the gold at the top, and put it back in for 14 days to let it be fixed again. This can happen without ceasing, and you will have a treasure as long as you live. **It is proven.**<note>original: "Probatum est."</note>

But where the earth is level, those vapors and smokes did not heap up, which is why no ore is found in those areas.

And as for the heaped-up earth, particularly where it was slimy, loamy <note>original: "lättig"; referring to clay-rich or sticky soil.</note>, and rich <note>original: "feyßt"; literally "fat," used to describe fertile or mineral-dense earth.</note>, the moisture passed through it from above, making it soft again. I, Georg Biltdorff, at this time Abbot of St. Morin, give testimony that Hieronymus Crinot—a born German who wandered for many years among the heathens in Egypt—was an excellent artist who possessed the true <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>original: "Stein der Weisen." The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>. He was adorned with great gifts, and he prophesied much; many of his prophecies were found to be the truth. As a pious Catholic Christian during his lifetime, he founded and built 1,300 churches and provided much for them, through which many rich alms are still distributed daily to the poor. This Crinot was able to <term>transmute</term> <note>original: "thingieren," derived from the Latin "tingere" (to dye or tint). In alchemy, it refers to the process of changing the nature and color of a metal.</note> all metals into the best gold by many thousand parts, and all precious stones to the highest degree. He kept himself simple and reclusive, letting nothing of his secret arts be noticed; he left behind only what he had written. He enjoyed the company of the religious orders and trusted them with much. After he traveled out of Germany, he came to Africa and died there.

After his death, many books were found in various languages and hidden scripts, containing great secrets. These were not the devil’s arts, as used by those who practice the <term>black arts</term> <note>original: "Schwartzkünstler," referring to necromancy or demonic magic.</note>, but were of a natural manner, without any superstition, so that no one could take offense at them. High-quality parchment made from the skin of a stillborn animal, traditionally used for the most important or sacred manuscripts.</note> with the following hidden script. There it is clearly to be seen what this righteous <term>first matter</term> <note>original: "prima materia." The formless, original substance that alchemists believed was the starting point for creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> is, through which, after its preparation, all common metals are transmuted into the best gold, remaining stable in all tests.

# Now the gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> is purified, dissolved with the prepared key into a spiritual essence, and also separated and coagulated.

Take the spiritual gold, with the glass well-sealed, and place it in clean, sifted ashes, buried as deep as the matter reaches. The ashes should be in a very thin earthenware vessel, and under the vessel, a lamp with six thick linen threads burning in oil. This should stand for thirty days and nights in such heat.

Afterward, one should make a wick of eight thick linen threads and hold it in steady heat for another thirty days; thereafter with ten thick linen threads for thirty days; then take twenty thick threads in the lamp and let it stand for fifteen days and nights. Then the spiritual gold will once again be <term>fixed</term> <note>stable and resistant to evaporation</note> and fire-resistant. It is thus coagulated again into a state of fixity; yet it is no longer a material gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> as it was before, which could be reduced to a physical body, but is instead a "Philosophical Gold." Of this, the masters say: our gold is not material, but rather an indestructible gold which penetrates all imperfect bodies.

Pour the aforementioned mercurial water over it until it is slightly covered. Place it in a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ"</note> for three days and nights, and this part will once again become spiritual

...onto 1,000 parts, and two parts of the Tincture are placed upon it while it is glowing, and then it is thrust back into the fire. In this way, it becomes the finest <term>gold</term> <note>original: ☉, the alchemical symbol for gold and the sun</note>, stable and enduring in all tests.

These following <term>augmentations</term> <note>alchemical processes used to increase the quantity or the "multiplication" of the alchemical Stone</note> I worked on in my youth and tested myself with them; almost all of them turned out well for me. The dissolution of metals, such as gold and silver, does not fail in their <term>spirituality</term> <note>original: "Geistlichkeit," referring to the state where a solid metal is turned into a vapor or "spirit" through chemical action</note>. And I say the augmentations produce <term>tinctures</term> <note>potent alchemical liquids capable of transforming base metals</note> when they proceed with their <term>resolution</term> <note>original: "Resolutierung," the breaking down of a substance into its component parts</note>. Whoever seeks otherwise in the <term>chemical art</term> <note>original: "Chymischen Kunst," an early term for alchemy</note>, and does not remain with the spiritual dissolution, is entirely and utterly mistaken; therein lies the foundation. It requires time to reach <term>fixity</term> <note>original: "fixitet," the state where a substance becomes stable and no longer evaporates or changes when exposed to high heat</note>, until it becomes resistant to fire again through its cooking. After that, nothing more can be spoiled, except that one must add its proper portion <note>original: "Gebürnuß," the required amount of "food" or additional material for the reaction</note> and let it cook further; thus the treasure increases without ceasing. Whether it is set with <term>gold</term> <note>original: ☉, the symbol for the sun and gold</note> or <term>silver</term> <note>original: "Luna," the moon and silver</note>, nature acts with great power, which no man can fathom. Our bodies will not rise if they do not rot in the earth, much less could they pass through closed doors in an instant. Likewise, if the <term>fixed</term> metals do not <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: "putrificieren," the alchemical stage of "death" or decomposition, usually marked by the color black, necessary for rebirth</note> and become spiritual, there is no hope that they should penetrate other metals.

And no imperfect body that is not fixed and produces smoke, such as lead, tin, or copper—even if they are putrefied and become living—will <term>penetrate</term> <note>the ability of the alchemical medicine to soak into and transform the entire mass of a base metal</note> as gold and silver do, which are perfect metals, pure in their essence, and otherwise permanent on their own in earthly fire, remaining stable without loss of their substance.

# Three Augmentations from Master Georg Bildorff’s Manuscript.

Let the brandy <note>distilled wine or spirits used as a solvent; original: "Brantenwein"</note> evaporate from it until it becomes a calx <note>a fine powder or oxide; original: "Kalch"</note>. This should be thoroughly sweetened <note>washed with water until all acidity or salts are removed; original: "außgesüßt"</note> and dried, then placed into a crucible. Set this in the ashes, just as was done with the gold, and let it stand according to the sequence of the fire for four weeks. Then, divide it into two equal parts. Grind into it a third part of <term>mercury</term> <note>original uses the symbol ☿; here referring to the "mercury of the body" or quicksilver</note>. Let it stand for three weeks following the order of the fire; then augment it again in the same way, and so on, continuously.

Now, take a third part of this gold augmentation—or of this augmentation for your sustenance—and let it melt with a <term>flux</term> <note>a substance added to promote melting; original: "Fluß"</note>. Refine it through lead <note>a process called cupellation, used to purify precious metals; original: "durchs Bley abtreiben"</note>, and it will be the finest gold, stable in all tests without any loss of substance.

And for whatever amount you have taken from the augmentation, grind an equal amount of <term>mercury</term> back into it. However, let it <term>fix</term> <note>become stable and resistant to fire; original: "figieren"</note> for three weeks so that you may benefit from it. And I tell you: you can create a complete <term>tincture</term> <note>a powerful alchemical substance capable of transmuting base metals or healing; original: "Tinctur"</note> from these augmentations, provided you rightly understand the dissolution of its substance, upon which the greater part of the work depends.

You can also make a running <term>mercury</term> out of tin and copper, and apply it to gold or silver just as well as any other running mercury. And even if such substances are not from <term>fixed bodies</term> <note>metals like gold and silver that do not oxidize or "vanish" in the fire</note>, they will nonetheless purify themselves alongside the pure bodies, so that they become tinctures and accomplish more than many would believe.

In the year 1510 <note>original: "Anno M. V. X."</note>, an old man of considerable age came to me and asked for soup at the monastery as a traveler. When he had eaten the soup, he asked for me, the Abbot, wishing to be in my presence. I ordered him to be brought to me and asked what he desired. He then thanked me for the monastery food and presented me with a gift of <term>mercury ore</term>, weighing about three pounds, just as it grows in the mountains. He said he had found this mine in the <term>Histerland</term> <note>original: "Hysterlandt," likely referring to Istria (Hister), a region famous for the Idrija mercury mines</note>, and that it was nothing but pure mercury—or what he called an "imperfect running metal" that the sun had not yet properly "cooked." Otherwise, he said, it would have become silver. And he knew very well how to separate it from the red earth...

## Preface to the Egyptian Royal
## Tincture.

<image-desc>Large decorative woodcut initial D, within which the letter is surrounded by intricate floral vine work and a central chalice or laboratory vessel from which wisps of steam or spirit emerge.</image-desc>
THIS Tincture was written by the great philosopher Hieronymus Erinot <note>The previous page identified him as "Crinot"; such spelling variations were common in early modern manuscripts.</note> with his own hand, using a secret alphabet. It is well-suited to be translated into English <note>original: "Teutſch" (German)</note>, though he did not write German very well. But this Tincture is a great <term>Arcanum</term> <note>A "secret" or "hidden" remedy; in alchemy, it refers to a powerful substance capable of transforming nature.</note>; it is not prepared with poison, as is done by some who seek a quick path to health by performing a dissolution with poison. This dissolution performed with this Tincture has a pleasant taste and is healthy to work with; the work is accomplished entirely with its own essence and tools. Nothing foreign is added to it except its own <term>Viscosa</term> <note>A "viscous" or "sticky" substance; here referring to the thick, essential matter of the base material.</note>. Once the <term>Solution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state, a fundamental step in the "Great Work" of alchemy.</note> has occurred, this Tincture is prepared over nine weeks. This was known to the pagan kings and others besides. How much more is it necessary for Christian Catholic kings and great potentates to know it? However, such workers of the Tincture should not be vagabonds, bunglers, or "whim-smelters" <note>original: "Grillenschmelzer"—a derogatory term for someone who pursues foolish, impractical fantasies (or "crickets in the head").</note> who search within common sulfurs <note>original: "Schwebeln"</note>, doing everything in haste and working only to become rich quickly. They wish to ruin much gold <note>symbol: ☉ (the Sun, representing gold)</note>, and when they fail to achieve such a Tincture, they claim the true Art must be a lie. They turn great lords away from a foundation that is certain and deceive them with their lying <term>Particularien</term> <note>Incomplete alchemical recipes that claim to transform only small amounts of metal, often used by frauds to get funding.</note> for many thousands of guilders <note>original: "Guldin"—a gold coin used across Europe.</note>. But if these lords had an experienced and faithful worker, they would obtain such Art at little cost. Then such a great lord—if he distributes his alms richly to the poor, so they might pray for him—shall be praised. Also, the Lord Jesus and his dear mother, the Virgin Mary, are praised through his good deed. And it is true: few artists are found who can work out a true Tincture; the reason is they have no understanding and do not know what wet or dry tinctures are.

<header>The Tincture of the Great King Sophar /</header>

### O Ref sonila sechdans. <note>This heading appears to be a cryptic cipher or phonetic code common in alchemical "Sophar" literature, likely masking a Latin or German instruction intended only for initiates.</note>

You should take good gold pyrites <note>original: "Goldkieß"; a mineral (likely iron or copper pyrites) containing traces of gold.</note> in which gold grows, which is full of sulfur; of this, take one pound, crushed small. Sublimate this <note>original: "auff jagen"; literally "to hunt up," meaning to drive a substance upward through heat in a sublimation vessel.</note> in an earthen instrument until you have enough, up to one pound. Grind it small and take half of it in a <term>cucurbit</term> glass <note>A gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation.</note>; upon this, you should pour an equal weight of the following "burning water." Let it stand for the dissolution of its volatility for 12 days and nights, and afterward distill it from the <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: "Bad Maris"; a water bath used to provide gentle, even heat.</note> until all the sulfur has risen over with the burning water. You should purify it by itself in the Bain-Marie; thus, the true Mercurial water is well-prepared by itself.

### Now follows the burning water.

Take 20 measures of good wine; distill it with a gentle fire in the cucurbit, well-sealed at the top with six layers of <term>chamois bladders</term> <note>original: "Gempsen Blatern"; animal membranes used to create an airtight seal (lute) at the joints of the glass apparatus to prevent vapors from escaping.</note>. Then take tartar <note>original: "Weinstein"; the potassium bitartrate sediment from wine barrels.</note> and <term>calcine</term> <note>To burn a substance to a white ash or powder.</note> it until it becomes beautifully white like a salt; dissolve it in water and coagulate it again. Do this for a third time, then it is right. Of this, take one good pound and put it into a cucurbit glass; then pour the distilled wine upon it and, as before, bind it with six layers of chamois bladders. Afterward, the water is distilled over the helm <note>The "helm" or alembic is the cap of the still that directs vapors into the cooling neck.</note>; that is the true, sharp burning water <note>A high-proof, rectified spirit of wine (ethanol).</note> which makes the <term>Gold</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note> entirely volatile for the apparatus. And continue further with the matter.

Take 8 parts of good gold and as much of the sulfur which you first sublimated in the instrument; use it to turn the <term>Gold</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note> into a <term>calx</term> <note>original: "Kalch"; the fine powder resulting from heating a metal.</note>. Take 6 parts of this in a cucurbit and pour upon it twice as much by weight of the burning water. Let it dissolve for 14 days and nights, well-sealed at the top. Keep it warm in <term>wine pomace</term> <note>original: "Weindröstern"; the skins and dregs of pressed grapes, which generate a steady, low fermentation heat.</note>; afterward, distill it from the Bain-Marie until everything has risen over into volatility. Then the secret <term>Mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿rius</note> is [ready].

<header>Described by Master Hieronymus Crinot. <note>Hieronymus Crinot was an alchemical author associated with the "Sophar" tradition and the "Testament of Cremer," focusing on the spiritual and physical transformation of metals.</note></header>

<sig>F 3</sig>

...in its first essence / the volatile instrument, and you should know / that you will complete the <term>tincture</term> <note>A potent substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold or silver.</note> in nine weeks.

Take these two parts of <term>Gold Calx</term> <note>original: "Goldtkalch"; gold that has been reduced to a fine powder through heating or chemical action.</note> remaining from the eighth part above; you should grind it in a small <term>cucurbit</term> <note>A gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation.</note>, then pour the volatile <term>Mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> upon it, just as it rose over with the burning water, and let the water cover it well. Afterward, place it in gentle warmth, let it stand in ashes <note>An ash bath provided a steady, indirect heat source for the glass vessel.</note> until it boils down, which happens in three weeks. In the last eight days, make the fire stronger so that it becomes quite dry. Then grind it again and put it into the <term>cucurbit</term>. Then add your volatile <term>Trial</term> <note>original: "Trialischen"; likely referring to a "Triple" water or a specific three-part solvent mentioned in this tradition.</note> water, and having moistened it, let it stand for eight days. If it is dry again, you should moisten it once more with the aforementioned water and let it stand for another eight days. The colors are visible signs, such as black, gray, dark-colored, yellow, white, and afterward red and beyond red. It receives all these colors in nine weeks. If you <term>bleach</term> <note>original: "blaichest"; to purify the substance until it reaches the "white" stage of the Great Work.</note> the work you have begun in this way with the aforementioned <term>Trial Water</term>, then the instrument is prepared for stability.

This is now the <term>Philosophical Gold</term>, which shall be dissolved with its burning <term>Mercurial water</term> as prepared above; this will soon boil down again, and then the true <term>tincture</term> is ready.

And I say that if it is brought several more times into the <term>spiritual state</term> <note>original: "Geistlichkeit"; in alchemy, this refers to the process of sublimation or distillation where a solid is made "spiritual" or volatile.</note>, it will <term>tinge</term> <note>original: "thingiert"; the act of the tincture transforming or coloring a base metal into gold.</note> several thousand parts.

# King Sophar’s Tincture, described by Master Hieronymus Crinot:

Take 20 parts of <term>fine gold</term> <note>pure gold, often refined through cupellation to ensure no other metals are present.</note>; let it melt into a <term>flux</term> <note>original: "Fluß"; the state of being molten or liquid under high heat.</note>. Afterward, take one part of this molten mixture and cast it into a <term>flux</term> of 40 parts of good gold. Let it sit for a while; this is the <term>Tincture</term> <note>This process of "multiplication" increases the potency and volume of the alchemical medicine.</note>. From this, take one part and project it onto 1,000 parts of <term>fine silver</term>, and it will become the best gold.

From the 40 parts, take one part and let 500 parts of <term>red copper</term> melt. Project the tincture upon it and let it stand for a good hour; thus it becomes high-quality and good gold without any <term>waste</term> <note>original: "abgang"; meaning the weight of the metal remains constant after transmutation.</note>.

Take one part from the fortieth part and let 800 parts of <term>English tin</term> <note>High-purity tin from Cornwall was highly prized by European alchemists for its consistency.</note> melt. Project the tincture upon it and let it stand for half an hour; thus it is good gold. This gold, when separated from other gold, is the best and most <term>malleable</term> <note>original: "geschmeydig"; a crucial quality for gold, indicating it is not brittle and can be worked by a goldsmith.</note> gold.

You should know that this tincture turns all <term>volatile metals</term> <note>Metals with lower melting points or those that "vanish" in fire, like tin or lead.</note> into the best metal <term>gold</term> <note>represented by the symbol $\odot$</note>; and I have described this secret tincture just as I brought it when I came out of <term>Egypt</term> <note>In alchemical literature, "Egypt" is often cited as the ancestral home of Hermetic wisdom to lend the text ancient authority.</note>.

The pagans did not do that to one another—from whom the secret arts mostly originated—for what the greatest among them knew, he shared with the needy.

The King summoned the same doctor who had presented the book to him and asked him if everything written in the book were true. He answered: "Most gracious King, I have compiled the very best pieces from many proven doctors and physicians and presented them to your Royal Majesty; I have tested none of them myself." Thereupon the King said to him: "You should have kept your lies for yourself."

Therefore, let great lords, both poor and rich, cherish this single piece, the <term>Suforethon</term>. Prepare it, and help the poor in their sickness. Amen.

# Salomon Trismosin’s description of nine Tinctures.

Take 15 parts of **Gold** and **Silver**, let them melt, and add one part of the **Vitriol Stone** <note>The "Vitriol Stone" refers to the purified, concentrated essence of metallic sulfates prepared on the previous page.</note> onto it; thus it becomes a Tincturing Essence. This <term>tinges</term> <note>To "tinge" means to transform the color and nature of a base metal into a noble one.</note> Iron, Silver, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: ☿</note>. Then have a very round rod forged from steel, and let it be heated until it glows intensely. For 50 parts [of metal], treat it with one part of this Tincture while it glows; hold it all in the fire, then quench it in urine, and it will become the finest gold.

Likewise, let 100 parts of Silver melt with this Vitriol Tincture; it will become the best Rhenish Gold. And it is exactly the same with common Mercury; know that it tinges according to which <term>Ferment</term> <note>An agent that "leavens" or directs the transformation; here, the metal added to the tincture determines the final output.</note> one desires or takes. If it is Silver, it becomes Silver; if it is Gold, it becomes Gold in its tincture.

### The second Tincture is as follows.

Next, take 15 measures or <term>Echtering</term> <note>A historical liquid measure used in German-speaking regions.</note> of the strongest old Austrian wine; distill this through a seven-fold Venetian paper so that it is entirely fiery and burning, and holds no water; when it is ignited, it should burn away completely. Then it is prepared for the extraction.

Now take one pound of the best <term>Mercury Sublimate</term> <note>original: *Mercurij Sublimati*; a highly toxic compound of mercury and chlorine, often used as a starting material in alchemical works.</note>, such as is sublimated in Venice. Grind this small with great caution, so that the dust does not enter your body. Before you grind it, you should eat a good piece of unsalted butter and drink <term>Wormwood wine</term> <note>Bitter wine infused with *Artemisia absinthium*; alchemists believed its bitterness protected the internal organs from toxic metallic vapors.</note> which is very bitter. Put this finely ground Sublimate into a Venetian <term>flask</term> <note>original: *Kolbenglaß*</note>; pour upon it 27 <term>Loth</term> <note>A unit of weight, roughly half an ounce.</note> of strong <term>Aqua Regis</term> <note>original: *Aqua regis*; literally "Royal Water," a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold.</note> in which one <term>Mark</term> <note>A unit of weight for precious metals, approx. 8 ounces.</note> of Hungarian fine gold has been dissolved. Set it to <term>putrefy</term> <note>In alchemy, "putrefaction" refers to a slow digestion or breakdown of substances using gentle heat.</note> with mild warmth in a <term>Water-bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum Mariae*</note> for six days and nights. Whatever rises to the top, pour it back onto the substance. After the six days, draw it off gently in an <term>Ash-bath</term> <note>original: *Eschen*; a method of heating a vessel by surrounding it with hot ashes for more intense heat than water.</note> until it is dry. Let it cool, break the glass, and grind it small. Put it into another glass, and pour the aforementioned <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum vini*; high-proof distilled alcohol.</note> over it so that it is well covered. Seal the glass at the top and let it stand in the <term>Water-bath</term> for 24 hours

## Now prepare the oily
## tincture thus.

Take it out of the water bath and place the glass in clean ashes with very gentle heat to **coagulate** <term>coagulate</term> <note>to solidify a liquid into a solid mass.</note> it into a stone. There is no danger in this method, unlike other tinctures worked with high **colors** <term>colors</term> <note>original: coloribus; likely referring to the volatile "red" stage of alchemy which can be explosive or easily ruined by too much heat.</note>. If the **alchemist** <term>alchemist</term> <note>original: Laborant</note> does not understand these steps, he will fail the entire Work.

## Thus it is tinged.

If so, it is entirely spiritualized <note>original: geistlich; meaning the fixed matter has been made volatile or refined into a "spirit"</note>.

### The eighth tincture in order.

Take ten **Loth** <term>Loth|A historical unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of fine silver; granulate it very small and put it into a good, durable glass. Pour 24 Loth of **aqua fortis** <term>Aqua fort|Nitric acid, a powerful solvent for silver</term> upon it; let it dissolve into a "water of the cloud" <note>likely a reference to the turbid or milky appearance of the solution as the metal dissolves</note>. Into this, add about 2 Loth of finely ground **sal ammoniac** <note>ammonium chloride, used to alter the properties of the acid</note>, and draw off the **aqua fortis** in ashes <note>evaporating the liquid using a heat-diffusing ash bath</note> until it reaches a thick consistency. Seal the top of the glass and place it in a **Bain-Marie** <term>Mariæ Balneum|A gentle water bath used for consistent, mild heating</term> with very mild warmth for 31 days and nights. 

Afterward, pour a very sharp **spirit of wine** <term>Spiritum vini|Highly concentrated alcohol or ethanol</term> over it so that it covers the matter well, and begin to distill from the water bath gently. Pour the distilled spirit back onto it and distill again; once more pour **spirit of wine** upon it and draw it off; finally, drive the heat strongly so that the silver rises together with the spirit over the helm <note>the "head" or cap of the distilling apparatus where vapors condense</note> of the glass. Let this rest for two days and nights, and the **viscous matter** <term>Viscosa|A sticky or thick residue</term> will settle at the bottom. Pour the water off carefully from the top and dry the **viscous matter**. 

Divide this into two equal parts. Take one part in a glass and place it in ashes; let it be **fixed** <note>original: figieren; the process of making a volatile substance resistant to the heat of fire</note> until it becomes entirely fire-proof. Then take this and grind it very small and mix the other half-part into it; place it again in a **violin** <note>original: Violin; a specifically shaped alchemical flask, often flattened or rounded</note> in ashes to fix and **coagulate** <note>to thicken or solidify into a stable form</note>; thus thereafter the tincture is prepared.

# Solomon Trismosinus’s description of nine Tinctures.

Of this [substance], take one part and cast it upon 100 parts of molten lead; that will all become a Tincture. From that, take one part for every 1000 parts of lead, let it remain in the flow for half an hour, and pour it out; thus it is the best silver, stable in all tests <note>referring to cupellation or other methods used by assayers to test purity</note>, and containing much gold.

Likewise, take purified copper according to common practice, 200 parts to one part of this aforementioned Tincture; let them melt together, and it will become pure Tincture. Of that, take one part for every 1000 parts of fresh copper, let it remain in the flow for a while, and pour it out; that is the highest silver that has ever been seen, very malleable; and you can proceed in this way with all metals, with <term>mercury|mercurius vivus; liquid mercury</term>, tin, and iron.

### The ninth and final Tincture.

Take half a pound of common cinnabar <note>mercury sulfide</note> and five **Loth** <term>Loth|A historical unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of washed iron sinter <note>iron scale or dross collected from a forge</note>; grind them small together and sublimate both in a sublimatory <note>a vessel used to heat a solid until it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again at the top</note>; thus the <term>mercury|mercurius vivus; liquid mercury</term> rises up entirely pure and shimmering. Of this, take 12 [parts] and 2 Loth of Hungarian gold; make an amalgam with it as goldsmiths do, and grind this small, and put it into a glass as follows. And take the soul of ancient <term>Saturn|lead</term>—understand me rightly, he who has all the planets within himself—take 6 Loth of his **Anima** <note>original: "Anima"; the "soul" or essential concentrated spirit extracted from the metal</note>, which should be a liquid; pour this onto the amalgam and seal the glass well at the top with a paper that you can later remove. Place it for 30 days in the following fire <note>referring to a specific heat arrangement described in the manuscript</note>, and every week look at what has risen to the top, and turn that gently back down to the material.

Thereafter, put the substance into a narrow glass for 50 days; thus it will turn black, then yellow, and thirdly red. Then take this along with the glass, place it in a strong fire for 15 days and nights; thus it will become blood-red, and in this way, the Tincture is prepared.

Of this, take one part and let 60 parts of purified <term>mercury|mercurius vivus; liquid mercury</term> be heated, and cast the part upon it; thus the mercury transforms into the best gold.

# The Red Eagle of Salomon Trismosin

### Now follows how the fixed red eagle is to be used.

Take 1,000 parts of running **mercury** <term>original: ☿; the planetary and chemical symbol for mercury</term> drawn from the mountains from its red earth <note>This likely refers to cinnabar, the red ore from which mercury is extracted.</note>. Let it flow in an earthen **crucible** until it begins to smoke, and then place one part of the **fixed eagle** <note>In alchemy, "fixed" refers to a substance that has been made resistant to the heat of fire so that it no longer evaporates.</note> upon it; that is all **Tincture** <note>A "tincture" is a concentrated substance capable of "dyeing" or transforming the nature of base metals into gold or silver.</note>. From this, take one part to 1,200 parts of **mercury** [☿]. Let it flow strongly and place the part upon it; this transforms the very heaviest metal into **gold**, the likes of which has never been seen. Though its body may be of a somewhat gray color, one should let it flow by itself in a great fire for nine hours; so it will gradually purify itself, and in these nine hours it will become so pure that it shines with a lovely redness and glows like a **carbuncle** <term>A legendary deep-red gemstone, often a garnet or ruby, believed to emit its own light in the dark.</term>.

### A wonder with this gold, as follows.

Take this shining gold, as it is in itself malleable and hammerable, and let 400 parts of **mercury** [☿] from the mountain flow until it becomes smoking. Take one part of the **gold** <term>original: ☉; the symbol for the Sun, representing gold</term>, let it flow by itself, and pour it while flowing into the smoking **mercury** [☿]. Let them circulate together for six hours, then pour it out; that is a superior gold of **28 degrees** <note>While modern gold is measured in 24 carats, alchemists often used "degrees" to describe a level of "perfection" or color intensity that surpassed natural gold.</note>. And let that be a wonder to me: that a malleable metal is thus **tinged** <note>original: "tingiert"; the process of alchemical transformation where a base metal takes on the color and properties of a noble one.</note>.

Now, if such a powder becomes white, or occurs in the form of a moisture: likewise take one part of the **fixed eagle** and cast it upon 1,000 parts of **tin**. Let it remain in the flow for six hours, then pour it out. That is a shining **white gold**, and this cannot be **refined** <note>original: "gradieren"; a metallurgical process to increase the purity or intensify the color of gold.</note> unless you then take one part of the **carbuncle-like gold** mentioned above and add it to 50 parts of the pale gold. Let them flow together for one hour; that is such a high gold which is stable in all tests.

# The Red Eagle of Salomon Trismosin.

### Electrum Soronella.

Take 4 **lots** <term>A traditional German unit of weight, approximately 15–17 grams.</term> of gold, filed as finely as possible, and 3 lots of common **cinnabar** <term>Mercury sulfide, a red mineral used here as a purifying agent.</term> <note>original: "Kromzinober"</note> which must be very red and well **sublimated** <term>The process of heating a substance to a vapor and cooling it back to a solid to purify it.</term>. Grind these two well together, place them on a flat plate, and slowly **reverberate** <note>To "reverberate" is to heat the mixture in a furnace where the flame or heat reflects off the roof onto the substance, driving off the cinnabar.</note> the cinnabar away from it, just as a skilled worker knows well how to do. Do this with fresh cinnabar a second and third time. Afterward, take the reverberated gold and place it in a **flask** <note>original: "Kolbenglaß"</note> that is not too tall; pour **Royal Water** <term>Known as *aqua regia*, a powerful mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold.</term> <note>original: "Aqua regis"</note> over it, which has previously been drawn from **sublimated mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio Sublimato"</note>. Place it in **Mary’s Bath** <term>A *Balneum Mariae* or water bath, providing gentle, indirect heat.</term>, and let it **putrefy** <term>The alchemical stage of breakdown or fermentation.</term> for fourteen days. Then, distill it gently up and down <note>A process of "circulation" or refluxing where vapors condense and flow back into the base.</note>, always pouring the water back in, until everything remains at the bottom.
Afterward, pour fresh [water] upon it and draw it off again to **clarity** <note>The original term "Helitet" is obscure; it likely refers to a state of transparency or a specific oily residue.</note>. Pour it back once more and drive it with strong heat so that the **Gold** [☉] rises over the **still-head** <note>original: "Helm" (helmet)</note> along with the water. Put all of this into a long-necked vial until the volatile Gold [☉] becomes **fixed** <note>Stable and resistant to heat.</note> once again. Put this fixed substance into a clean glass, and pour over it the red **Oil of the Eagle**, as named above. Let these coagulate together into a reddish-brown stone; thus the Electrum is prepared.

# Concerning Several Noble Gemstones which are highly graded in this Oil.

Take polished <term>The original "balliert" refers to stones that have been shaped and smoothed.</term> gemstones which are somewhat dark at the base or the bottom, such as an amethyst; let them lie in this oil for one month in gentle heat. Likewise, a well-polished **crystal**, if it experiences this oil in the heat, will become the best **diamond** <note>The original "Demůt" is a variation of "Demant," the archaic term for diamond.</note> in three weeks. And I say that all gemstones which lie in this oil for over 24 hours in gentle heat will be very highly **graded** <term>In alchemy, "grading" is the process of improving a substance's quality, color, or "dignity."</term>, so that they outshine all others of their kind.

# Of the Atolic Eagle.

### Thus proceed with this Atolic Eagle, as follows.

Take the best Austrian spirit of wine <note>original: "Spiritum vini"; high-proof alcohol or ethanol</note>, and put into it a good sal ammoniac <note>original: "Salmiar"; ammonium chloride, often used as a flux or solvent in alchemy</note> in a glass cucurbit <note>original: "cucurbitam"; a gourd-shaped flask used in distillation</note>. Upon this, place a six-fold Venetian paper <note>High-quality, thick paper used for filtration</note> and a helm <note>The top part of a still, also called an alembic</note> over it. Let it rise very gently in a sand bath <note>A container of sand heated to provide even, moderate warmth</note> into a receiver glass <note>original: "Fürlegglaß"; the vessel that catches the distilled liquid</note> until the spirits of wine have come over; then the water is prepared.

Take four lots <note>A "Loth" is a historical unit of weight, roughly 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of this glittering, golden magnesia <note>Not modern magnesium, but a "mother" mineral found in gold mines</note> and put them into a cucurbit glass with a long neck, as the experienced laboratory workers well know. Pour the prepared spirit of wine over it and seal it well at the top; place it in gentle, warm ashes for one hour. Thus the coagulate <note>The solid matter</note> dissolves into a black oil and is entirely and completely destroyed as a physical body, becoming a spiritual essence. Thereafter, place a helm upon it with a four-fold paper in between, but let it proceed slowly, so that the spirit of wine rises away and the magnesia remains in the form of a liquor <note>A liquid substance</note>, which is volatile. This is one of the greatest secrets <note>original: "Arcanen"</note> in the chemical art; mark this well.

Now take then one lot of gold leaf <note>original: "Aurum foliatum"</note> from the gold-beaters; add this to the Atolic Eagle and seal the glass with the seal of Hermes <note>original: "Sigillo hermetis"; an airtight, philosophical seal often made by melting the glass shut</note>. Let it coagulate by half in subtle ashes, set in gentle warmth. Let it stand for fourteen days, and thus the Atolic Eagle has made the gold <note>original: symbol for gold ☉</note> entirely volatile—turning it into a fleeting essence. Watch carefully that nothing rises too high, for this Atolic bird flies with its own kind and spreads its wings in its power, appearing in various colors which are wondrous to behold.

Now let it stand in its own constellation <note>Referring to the internal celestial or energetic influence within the vessel</note> with a very small increase of the fire for fourteen days; then you will see the black-speckled eagle, as the colors all follow one after another in the order described. Proceed thus to the end.

The first color: Will manifest as a mixed red.

The second and third colors: Will be blue and partly green in the neck of the glass.

Let them stand therein for 16 hours, and they will become the best **Gold** <note>symbol: ☉</note>, constant in all tests. And I tell you that this oily Tincture is a very fast-penetrating hellish fire. You can lay other fresh silver leaves therein, and continue to use it in this way.

### Now follows the fourth Tincture.

Take Roman Vitriol <note>original: "Vitrioli Romani"; iron or copper sulfate.</note> and Saltpeter <note>original: "Salis nitri"; potassium nitrate</note>, of each one and a half pounds; <term>Sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "Salarmoniac"; ammonium chloride</note> 8 <term>Loth</term> <note>A unit of weight, roughly 15 grams.</note>; and one pound of crushed bricks. From these, burn an <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>original: "Aqua fort"; literally "strong water," a corrosive acid used to separate metals.</note> according to the proper custom. Take 8 Loth of <term>corrosive sublimate</term> <note>original: "Mercurij Sublimati"; a highly toxic form of mercury chloride.</note>—as it is made in Venice—and guard yourself against its poisonous smoke. Put this into a cucurbit and pour the prepared Aqua fortis upon it. Draw it off strongly so that the **Mercury** <note>symbol: ☿</note> mixes well with the Aqua fortis; then the <term>Aqua regia</term> <note>original: "Aqua regis"; literally "royal water," a mixture of acids that can dissolve gold.</note> is ready.

Now take 8 Loth of finely filed **Gold** <note>symbol: ☉</note> and four Loth of common <term>cinnabar</term> <note>original: "Zinober"; mercury sulfide.</note>. Set them on plates to <term>reverberate</term> <note>original: "reuerberirn"; a process of heating where the flame is deflected onto the material.</note> until the cinnabar is drawn off and burned away. Then take fresh cinnabar and do it once more; thus the **Gold** <note>symbol: ☉</note> will be "opened" <note>An alchemical term meaning the metal has been made chemically reactive or reduced to its primary state.</note>. Take that, put it into a cucurbit, and pour the Aqua fortis upon it so that it is well covered. Draw it off in a sand bath very gently until the half-part. Afterward, pour the drawn-off water back onto it and distill it off again. Reiterate this pouring on and drawing off 34 times. Finally, drive the heat very strongly so that it <term>precipitates</term> <note>original: "præcipitir"; forms a solid powder at the bottom of the glass.</note>.

Grind this precipitate small, put it into a clean glass, and seal it well at the top. Set it in moist <term>horse manure</term> <note>original: "Roßmist"; a standard laboratory method for providing a constant, gentle, natural heat through fermentation.</note> for twelve days and nights.

### The Tesolon of Salomon Trismosinus.

God gave it to them, even as evil men; they practiced all evil lusts therewith, for their hearts were full of villainy, and they spoke all manner of evil against their neighbors. Set it in gentle heat so that it coagulates well into a stone, yet does not rise up. And you should know that the work can and must happen in a single glass, if the glass is of good quality. Take this stone within the glass and set it to putrefy in horse manure; let it stand until the stone turns to water and is resolved. <image-desc>Large decorative woodcut initial 'V' featuring intricate scrollwork and floral patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>Wonder upon wonder I have seen among the crude, uncomprehending artists and laborers in this <term>Chemical Art</term> <note>Alchemy.</note>, for they have sought <term>Tinctures</term> <note>The "Medicine" or substance capable of transforming base metals into gold.</note> in common Salt, in extracted <term>Salt of Tartar</term> <note>original: "WeinsteinSaltz"; potassium carbonate produced from wine lees.</note>, in animal and human bones, and also in many kinds of earths and sulfurs; in lead, tin, copper, iron, <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿.</note>, and all those which are the fuming metals. Whoever can skillfully separate it from the <term>Antimonial Sulfur</term> <note>The volatile, combustible principle within the ore.</note> has the means to sustain himself. It is called *sol obscurum* <note>Latin: "hidden gold."</note> because it is not visibly noticed within the Antimony; the reason for this is that the quantity of sulfur in the Antimony covers the gold. And wherever the Antimony rises in the fire, it always carries this *sol obscurum* away with it, and it is also called *sol eleuatum* <note>Latin: "elevated" or "sublimated" gold.</note> by many philosophers.

I say further: if the Antimony were not mixed with gold, then <term>mined gold</term> <note>original: "Bergkgolt"; natural gold found in the earth.</note> would not become so pure and clear, nor reach such a high <term>grade</term> <note>original: "Gradt"; degree of fineness or purity.</note> when poured through it. For the "elevated gold," alongside the Sulfur of Antimony, tinges common mined gold so highly that it lacks nothing in any <term>trial</term> <note>Testing of metal purity.</note> and stands perfectly in all its power.

Therefore, a tincture can certainly be drawn from Antimony because the Gold is within it; otherwise, if the gold were not there, there would be little hope to be found in it or in its sulfur.

Take the glass, seal it well at the top, and set it on very gentle heat in an ash bath. Let it slowly solidify into a stone. Afterward, take the glass and place it with the material back into moist **horse manure** or a **water bath** so that it dissolves <note>original: "resoluiere."</note> again. Then solidify it once more. Continue this process of dissolving and solidifying until it no longer wishes to solidify and remains an incombustible oil. ## Of Geroton Salomon Trismo-
## sinus.

This **Tincture** <term>a potent alchemical substance capable of transmuting base metals</term> is to be brought through its **solution** <term>the process of dissolving a solid into liquid</term> to such a state that it ultimately **transmutates** <note>original: "tingiert"</note> 1000 parts of base metals into the finest **gold** <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note>. # The Sal Ammoniac Water.

Take 2 pounds of **Sal Ammoniac** <term>ammonium chloride; a salt used in alchemy to help dissolve metals and minerals</term>; dissolve this in a wine, let it stand overnight, and you will find **crystals** at the bottom. Divide this into two parts; however, first let it turn into water <note>original: "zu Wasser werden"; likely referring to deliquescence, where the salt absorbs moisture from the air until it liquefies</note>. Put one part into a **receiver glass** <term>a vessel used to collect the condensed liquid during distillation</term>; drive the other part into the receiver out of a **boiling flask** <term>a round glass vessel with a long neck, used for heating</term>. ## Trismosin’s Treatise/

# On all kinds of sulfurous pyrites, also on firestone or gunstone; how they are to be used in the chemical art, and what benefit they provide, whereby much gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> is obtained in some cases, so that a poor fellow may well support and sustain himself; therein are found several <term>particulars</term> <note>specific recipes for partial transmutations rather than the full creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

### This is a little trial piece as follows.

Take sulfurous gun-pyrites, roast it until red, and take raw antimony and raw <term>tartar</term> <note>original: "tartarum"; potassium bitartrate, often collected from wine casks.</note>, three and a half <term>Loth</term> <note>A German unit of weight equal to about half an ounce (approx. 15 grams).</note> of each, and 1 Loth of steel filings; grind everything small together. After that, proceed again with the silver as before; let the regulus be refined again through lead, and then you have fixed silver.

# The Flux.

<margin>Note well</margin> Take one <term>Loth</term> <note>A German unit of weight equal to approximately 15 grams.</note> of silver-litharge <note>original: "☽ glett"; the oxidized lead byproduct from silver refining.</note>, four Loth of common salt <note>original: "Sal commune".</note>, two Loth of red <term>tartar</term> <note>Potassium bitartrate deposits from wine barrels.</note>, and half a Loth of iron filings. ## 5. A Feat of Art with Silver.

Take sulfurous pyrite <note>original: "Büchsenkiß"; likely iron pyrites or marcasite used as a source of sulfur and iron.</note> and common shop-sulfur; mix them together, four Loth of each. <term>Calcine</term> <note>To heat a substance until it is reduced to a powder or "ash."</note> fine silver <note>original symbol: ☽</note> (which contains no gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>) with this. ## 7. Another excellent part-for-part process, and it has been found correct fifteen times.

<margin>for my [records]</margin>
**R**ecipe [Take]: Sulfur, pyrite <note>original: "Büchsenkiß"; iron pyrites, often used as a source of sulfur in alchemical works.</note>, and raw antimony, each finely crushed, four <term>Loth</term> <note>A German weight equal to about 15 grams.</note> each. Prepare with copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note> sheets, layer upon layer <note>original: "stratum super stratum".</note>; let it calcine <note>Heat until reduced to a powder.</note> gently for five hours. Take these sheets, grind them small, and mix in an equal weight of red-calcined pyrite. Put this into a glass flask; over it, pour a strong Jasoron <note>A specific alchemical term for a potent solvent or acid, likely a form of aqua regia or nitric acid.</note> so that it rises well above it by two fingers' breadth. Let it stand in gentle heat for 26 hours; thus the extract is ready.

<margin>A</margin>
<margin>Sublimated mixture</margin>
Now take gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> calx <note>A powder produced by heating metal.</note> which has been precipitated through the Jasoron and prepared with sulfur, as mentioned above, one Loth. Take three <term>Quintlein</term> <note>A weight equal to about 4 grams.</note> of Suginol mercury <note>original symbol: ☿; "Suginol" is a deck-name or "cover name" for mercury.</note> rubbed into the gold calx; put it together into a glass flask <note>original: "Cucurbit".</note>. Pour the extract over it, one Loth of the sulfur [extract], and dissolve one Loth of fine silver <note>original symbol: ☽</note> in the Jasoron. Pour this in as well and distill it off by [the depth of] nine finger-widths; pour the water back on and distill it off again. Do this until all the liquid remains fixed upon it and the material becomes a precipitate. Grind this small and mix it with an equal weight—measured by the full swing of the scale—of the flux made with litharge <note>original: "Glett"; lead oxide.</note>, common salt <note>original: "Sal cōmune".</note>, and <term>tartar</term> <note>original: "Tartaro"; potassium bitartrate.</note>. Let it melt gently for a quarter of an hour and drive off the <term>regulus</term> <note>original: "König"; the lump of pure metal found at the bottom of a crucible after smelting.</note>; thus the "part-for-part" <note>An operation where a portion of gold "multiplies" or converts a portion of base metal or silver into more gold.</note> is all gold. An <term>aqua regis</term> <note>A mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold.</note> is better for the first extract for this reason.

## 8. The third part-for-part.

**T**ake this extract; pour it over a sublimated cinnabar <note>Mercury sulfide.</note>. Precipitate it with this cementing "part-for-part" of gold and silver. Whatever it takes into itself remains as gold; the rest is found in the powder, which is reduced with the litharge flux.

# The Golden Fleece of Theophrastus Paracelsus / is a dialogue about <term>Alchemy</term> <note>Alchemy: A historical philosophical and protoscientific tradition focused on the transformation of matter, particularly the turning of base metals into gold and the pursuit of universal cures.</note> / in which Theophrastus instructs Chrysophilus <note>original: "Chrisophilum." <image-desc>An ornate woodcut initial 'I' decorated with intricate vine, floral, and scrollwork motifs, spanning the height of the first six lines of the paragraph.</image-desc>

I cannot sufficiently complain / and weep for this everlasting and common misery of mankind / when I see that all things / in which there is hardly a shadow of the good / are so burdensome and confused / that hardly one in a thousand can obtain them / and even when they have been brought within reach / they escape us quite swiftly; conversely, however, evil and dangerous things / weigh upon us with every hardship / so persistently / that we can think nothing else / than that they are designed for our destruction / for in a blink of an eye we are ruined—misery / poverty / sickness / and pain fall upon us in heaps. But for us to be blessed / for us to be rich / or for us to become healthy / for that we require many years / and that we should lack for nothing / that hardly happens to us in a hundred years. As far as my own affairs are concerned / I am entirely in that same state and condition / and because from my youth I have desired nothing more (of which I am ashamed to openly admit) / than that I might become powerfully rich / that same thirst I have for gold / has completely captivated and corrupted me / and yet to obtain it I have until now received no perfect instruction / and because I have doubted / that it would ever turn out according to my wish—

# A Conversation about Alchemy.

## Chrisophilus.

Indeed, through your help I hoped to achieve that same peace; in your hands stands my well-being and salvation. If you are now willing to be helpful to me, I hope or rather I know, that I shall see to it that we both, in a short time, shall be the highest among the people.

## Theophrastus.

For my part, my dear Chrisophilus, I will—as far as it depends on me—not refuse to stand by you with all my advice and help (provided that such a thing does not involve obvious danger to myself). But explain briefly what the business and the matters are.

## Chrisophilus.

You will, without doubt, have heard how great a loss and damage I have suffered—not only in riches and in money, but also in time (which is the most precious thing)—on account of this art, which the learned call <term>Chymia</term> <note>Alchemy or early chemistry.</note>, having applied myself to it and lost much. I am also ashamed to confess—though I cannot deny it—how miserably I have been deceived by that perverted sort of people, indeed those rogues, who boast and preen as Alchemists and <term>Disciples of the Philosophers</term> <note>original: "Jünger der Philosophorum." This refers to those who claimed to follow the teachings of ancient natural philosophers like Aristotle or Hermes Trismegistus to create the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. And the heaviest burden of all is how severely I have harmed my health from the stinking soot and most gruesome tastes <note>Likely referring to the toxic fumes and metallic flavors inhaled or ingested during experiments.</note> which I endured and took in within the lowest caverns and vaults, where I performed hidden labor like the <term>Troglodytes</term> <note>original: "Tragloditer." A reference to legendary cave-dwellers; Chrisophilus is describing his windowless, smoke-filled laboratory as a subterranean cave.</note>. The total loss and damage of all these things is so great that even the profits which might be scraped together from this art—even if all the works were successfully completed—could not be reckoned against the loss.

### Theophrastus.

Ha, ha, ha! I could laugh myself sick if I hadn't already had a taste of that very thing—even if I were otherwise unaware of your affairs. For when I passed by your **little house** in the garden last month, I noticed such a stinking and coal-black smoke coming out of a **little vault** you have underground. I could have imagined and believed it was the **jaws of hell** itself, in which the **Devil's mother** cooks porridge for her children. 

But so that I would not form an unfair opinion of your prudence, I was conflicted. Firstly, there is your respectable authority; next, the fact that you are born of the highest lineage here; then your advanced age, which has experience in many things; and finally, so many obvious examples and instances from which I would have thought you’d have become wise and cautious by observing the danger and damage of other people. Therefore, I could not persuade myself that you should apply your senses to such things which are obviously fraught with damage and loss—much less listen to the most harmful deceivers and rogues, who are themselves the desecrators and mockers of the **true art** <note>The "true art" refers to legitimate alchemy or natural philosophy, as opposed to the "sophistry" of fraudulent gold-makers.</note>.
