Whatever remains hanging on the wire, beat it thin upon an anvil; thus you will soon see whether it is still brittle or not.

If it seems to you to still be brittle, add more <term>tin <note>original: ♃</note></term> or <term>copper <note>original: ♀</note></term> to that which you have set to be tinctured; then it will become fine and malleable. And note well this aforementioned secret regarding the three days and nights: reveal it to no man. Write it upon the tablet of your heart, so that the godless, proud, and haughty may not reach a perfect end. Remember that all of this is a gift from God; if you reveal it, you will see that God will punish you.

But what is the cause that it does not mix or unite with the metals in the first flux, even though it is itself of a metallic type and nature? It is now so noble and worthy that it will no longer mix with the coarse metals without a mediating agent; for a thing that has once cast off its impurity mixes difficult-

<margin>16. Earth is the mother of the elements, for from earth they proceed, and to earth they return. If you have now completed your Medicine and wish to work it out toward the **Red** <note>The "Red" or *Rubedo* is the final stage of the alchemical Great Work, signifying the highest potency of the Philosopher's Stone</note>, stay persistent with your heat until the white color begins to turn into a **Citrine** <term>color <note>a yellowish-orange hue representing the transitional stage between the white and red works</note></term> again. It will become all the more **fixed** <note>In alchemy, "fixity" refers to a substance's ability to withstand the heat of fire without evaporating or changing</note>, for you can spoil nothing by this. Rather, keep it always in its steady heat—as in the beginning, so also in the end. Then, when it is finished and gives no smoke upon the **silver sheet** <note>original: "Luna blech"</note>, keep whatever you wish to use for the silver. Note that the Medicine requires no further preparation for healing <note>likely referring to the "curing" or transformation of metals</note>. But for the **Tincture**, you must proceed exactly thus with 1,000 parts of <term>calcined gold <note>original: "Calcis solis", gold reduced to a fine powder through heat or chemical action</note></term> to one part of the Medicine, driven together on a clear, clean **refining stone** <note>original: "Treibstein", a cupel or stone used in the assaying and refining of precious metals</note>.

### Concerning the furnace follows hereafter:

Now I will tell you about the furnace: how large, high, and wide it must be, and what kind of fire you should then place in it, and also how you should govern that same Philosophical Fire.

<margin>17</margin>
Rosarius says: The fire of dung <note>original: "Ignis fimi"; composting manure was used by alchemists to provide a low, constant, and moist heat over long periods</note> is the agent in the work of the digestion of our stone. Nor is the fire of Mary's Bath <term>effective <note>original: "Balnei Mariæ"; a water bath or bain-marie, which alchemists found too hot or too "dry" for this specific stage</note></term>, even if very well-tempered; whence Alchidius <note>a reference to a medieval alchemical authority, possibly Al-Kindi</note> says: To cook with the fire which I shall show you; our fire is to hide the matter in moist horse dung; it is the moist and dark fire of the wise, and it is hot in the second and moist in the first degree <note>referring to the system of "degrees" of heat and moisture used in Galenic medicine and alchemy</note>, the property of which fire is not to destroy the oil or the Matter, but to increase it because of its temperate moisture; for only that equal and temperate heat is of such a kind as is supremely necessary in the generation of this art.

The furnace should be made 9 measure-feet long and 5 high; it should be divided in the middle so that these two parts are as wide as each other, namely each compartment 4 feet wide inside and 5 feet high; thus it has the correct size, which may then be called a true Philosophical Furnace. Then fill such compartments with horse dung in which there is no straw; when they are thus full, let them stand for 5 days; and on the 5th day, place the Matter into one part (as you have learned before in the Practice); the other part you must <term>renew <note>original: "Renouieren"</note></term> with new, fresh horse dung, namely in this way: in the middle you must take out the "burnt" <note>meaning spent or cooled</note> dung from top to bottom, about a good hand's breadth from the floor of the furnace, and fill it again with fresh dung as said above; so it begins to heat up, and on the 3rd day, it also reaches its proper warmth, and

When it has stood for two and a half hours <note>original: "drithalb Stund"; an archaic German expression meaning "the third hour is half-finished," or 2.5 hours</note>, make a hole so that the glass flask may go inside; set it right in the middle of the dung, ensuring it stands exactly in the center of the furnace, and close it up again well with the dung. Treat the other part in the same way from those hours onward: take out the aforementioned dung in the manner described before, put fresh dung back in its place, and let it stand again for two and a half hours to begin heating. Then move the glass across. This is what is called: cook, cook, and cook again <note>original: "coque, coque, & iterum coque"</note>. And take great care that you move it forward every 3rd day, and immediately renew the other part; in this way, five days are spent in each part of the furnace. Note: you must manage the renewal as mentioned above. And when you now wish to corrupt <note>in alchemy, "corruption" is the necessary breakdown or "death" of a substance before it can be "reborn" or transmuted into a higher form</note> the metals, you must take a vial as mentioned in the *Practica* <note>referring to a practical instruction manual or a specific section of this work</note>, which has a long neck and is sealed as follows: the neck of the vial must protrude out the top by about two fingers or a hand's breadth. However, if you are purifying our mercury <note>symbolized in the text as ☿</note> and want to place it in its vessel with the sphere as you were taught above, then the board lying on the dung needs no hole; rather, the more snugly it lies upon it, the better it is. Note that you should place our mercury together with the wooden sphere right in the middle of the dung, packed all around with dung. Also, place a thick board over the dung in each part of the furnace so that it closes down fine and tight upon it; in this way, the vaporous fumes remain within the dung <note>original: "Fimo"; Latin for dung or manure</note>. This is the Philosophical Furnace and Fire, and nothing else should be done from the beginning to the end.

# For the Tincture <note>original: "pro tinctura"</note>

When you want to **hermetically seal a vial** <note>original: "Sigillieren"; the act of creating an airtight "Seal of Hermes" by melting the glass or using a special sealant</note> **or a glass sphere**,
then you must have glass stoppers that fit exactly over them,
which cannot fall inside. And when you close the stopper,
strew the powder finely all around it to the thickness of a knife’s
blade. Build a brick fire around the neck of the glass; this
must be buried in a hollow hearth, so that only the mouth
sticks out by two fingers’ width. Then gradually increase the heat
until the powder begins to flow. When that happens
and the stopper begins to sink, then quickly and nimbly remove
the glowing coals and simply place a glowing crucible <note>original: "Digel"</note> over
the melted glass and let it cool by itself; otherwise,
if the crucible were not glowing hot, the glass would
shatter.

Now begin in the name of God your Creator,
the Almighty, to accomplish the hidden mystery which
God has planted into Nature and given to the human
race for their knowledge, through which they may recognize
how wonderfully all things are created, and how all
earthly races are born, as a testimony to all Christian
people and as a comfort to all the weak and troubled. For
everything that has ever been created, and is still daily born,
must pass away and rot <note>original: "verfaulen"; referring to the alchemical stage of putrefaction or "Nigredo," where matter must break down to be transformed</note>, so that it may all rejoice again in
its new birth—which shall be multiplied <note>original: "multiplicirt"; the alchemical process of increasing the quantity and power of the stone</note> in the future—
and each may bring forth its own kind and form from its seed.
For everything that is born and created has no rest,
because Nature works forever to increase and multiply
its own kind, for which purpose it was created and ordained—
all for the good of the human race. Therefore, learn
well from this and pray to God for wisdom and understanding,
and also that He may come to your aid at the beginning of
this high, Divine, and Laudable Art <note>original: "Kunst"; a standard term for the Great Work of Alchemy</note> (to the praise of God and the
improvement of your neighbor) and that He may grant His
Divine blessing to help you advance and reach completion.

# The Process <note>original: "Processus"</note>

If you wish to ask for and receive such wisdom from God, then ask from the heart as a sinner for His divine blessing and prosperity, so that you may receive such divine gifts more worthily—not with pride or arrogance—so that you do not bring upon yourself wrath and eternal damnation for the unmerited favor which God gives you. Rather, begin this blessed work in the name of the Almighty and for the benefit and service of all pious Christians, for the elevation and building up of the Christian religion, and to be a rescuer and helper against the unbelievers. Have no desire or pleasure in joining the company of the ungodly or opposing the righteous and the needy; instead, stretch out your hand to offer your bread with kindness, so that after this life you may attain eternal life from God—the crown and joy of eternal salvation <note>original: "Seeligkeit"</note>. May God help us all to this, Amen.

In this little book, I have shown and taught you the right path in the best and shortest way: how, where, and when you should make and prepare the Philosopher's Stone <note>original: "Philosophischen Stein"</note>, which the ancient philosophers made with their own hands but kept hidden with great diligence from unwise and proud people. Therefore, pray to God for His Spirit, that He may enlighten you and sharpen your understanding, and likewise open your eyes so that you may thank and recognize God with a sincere heart. Then you may see the great wisdom hidden in this Art <note>original: "Kunst"; the historical term for the practice of alchemy</note>, which from eternal times could never be fully fathomed by any master. Yes, good Master, I do not understand the words you have spoken.

# Dialogue

From that time when I first began to research this noble Art, I have always started with a whole heart to pray for the **Solution of the Philosophers** <term>Philosophers' Solution: The crucial first step in the "Great Work" where the physical matter is dissolved into its liquid, spiritual essence.</term>, and yet I was never able to obtain this from any living person. But now I know it all, for he who has eyes of understanding sees that all the labors in the entire wide world are full of error and blinded in their wretched ignorance. For some work with **Salt** <note>original: *Sali*</note>, some with **Alum**, some with **Borax**, some with human urine, and some with eggs, some with strong waters <note>Corrosive acids used to dissolve metals.</note>, **Marcasites** <note>Iron pyrites or other metallic minerals often mistaken for gold or silver ore.</note>, and the like. From all of these, I recognize—and by your grace—that the **Tincture** <note>The final medicine or substance used to perform transmutation.</note> of our Stone is drawn solely from the **Mercury of the Wise** <note>original: *☿ der weisen*; alchemists believed their "Mercury" was a secret substance, not the common quicksilver found in mines.</note>, which is not the common mercury, nor that which is drawn out of the earth or dug from it (though they also take that mercury), but rather our Mercury is of the Body, Soul, and Spirit. And you, my Master, have taught me this at the beginning of this little book, and I see that in all the world there is no other thing but this Stone alone, known only to us. And dear Master, whatever your dignity and generosity commands in which I may be pleasing to you and serve you in return, that I will gladly do and be your servant.

And son, give God the honor, for He is a wellspring and origin of all good, and in Him is kept all treasure and wisdom; may His name be blessed from world to world. Amen.

->An Example of the Philosophical Art<- <note>original: *Exemplum artis Philosophiæ*</note>

# An Example of the 
## Philosophers' Art

An Old Man <note>In alchemy, the "Old Man" often represents the *prima materia* or the metal lead, which must undergo a symbolic "death" or dissolution to be transformed.</note> near death, in whom the Natures are perfectly put together or joined, and united: the Earth, the Water, his Fire, and Air; and all these are found in the **Lead** <note>original: *Bley*; here referring to the "Lead of the Philosophers," a secret starting material, not necessarily common plumbing lead.</note>. With this, the gates of the Art are opened. As Hermes <term>Hermes Trismegistus: The legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy and author of the Hermetic Corpus.</term> and his ancestors say: **Take** <note>original: *R.*, the standard abbreviation for the Latin *Recipe*.</note> the Stone that hangs over the sea; it is an Old White Wax. A child—his name is called "Overcoming"—with the same [substance], kill the living and quicken the dead things; and he has life and death, and this and that from the Sunrise <note>The East.</note> and Sunset <note>The West.</note>. With this, you shall possess the Art.

In this, the Arabs have become weary <note>Likely referring to the great medieval Arabic alchemists like Jabir ibn Hayyan (Geber) or Rhazes, implying that even they found these secrets difficult to master.</note>. # Chapter six. <note>original: Caput sextum.</note>

And so it is manifest / that our Stone is out of the 4 elements / for the soul / the spirit and the **body** <note>original: Corpus; refers to the solid material state of the matter</note> / are our Stone (as the **philosophers** <note>original: Philosophi</note> say / it becomes with one thing / and out of one thing / and in that they speak the truth / for the entire **Mastery** <note>original: Meisterschafft; a term for the "Great Work" of alchemy</note> / comes out of our Water / that **dissolves** <note>original: Solvirt</note> all **bodies** / and **calcines** <note>original: Calciniert; reduces to a fine powder through heat</note> them again to earth / and transforms them to ashes / and our Water **whitens** <note>original: dealbirt; refers to the Albedo or "whitening" stage of the work</note> and makes pure / and makes hot / and **purifies** <note>original: Mundificirt</note>, **as Morienus testifies** <note>original: teste Morieno; Morienus was a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist</note> / who says / that **Azoth** <note>A universal solvent or "mercury of the philosophers" thought to contain the beginning and end of the work</note> and the fire / whiten and purify our **Laton** <note>original: Latonem; an alchemical term for an impure metal, often copper-like, that must be cleansed</note> / which is the impure **body** / or our first black earth.

**Azoth** is **quicksilver** <note>original: Argentum viuum</note> / and the fire is the **ferment** / which unites the **Azoth** with the form and **body** / in such a connection / that in such a union they may never more be separated by any destruction / and this union is our **sublimation** <note>original: Sublimation; while in modern chemistry this means turning a solid to gas, alchemists used it to mean the "uplifting" or refining of a substance</note> / yet not as the fools think / who take calcined **bodies** / and mix them with **sublimated spirits** / such as **mercury** or **arsenic** / and make a strong fire under them / so that they elevate the lime <note>The powdered residue of calcination</note> / and say / those are **sublimated bodies** / and have deceived themselves in this / for the **bodies** become much more impure than before / and they wish to make from contemptible things something higher and greater / and to transform them into a pure **nature** through mastery.

And therefore our **sublimation** <note>original: Sublimierung</note> is nothing other / than making subtle / and all this is done by our Water alone / thus you should understand our **sublimation** / for very many have been deceived in this / for our Water / kills and makes alive again / and gives the colors in manifest appearance / first in the black color / and when that happens / so that the living dies / and that which was a water / becomes into

Concerning the Stone <note>original: De lapide</note>

[It] transforms the earth / and is the first composition / and the earth is [made] solely out of the dryness of the body / and is also called Magnesia <note>In alchemical texts, "Magnesia" refers not to the modern element magnesium, but to a mysterious, foundational material—often a dark or silvery substance—believed to hold the potential for transformation.</note>.

Rasis <note>Rhazes (c. 865–925 AD), a Persian polymath and one of the most cited authorities in medieval alchemy</note> says / take our lead / or our Magnesia / or lead <note>original: plumbum</note> / or sulfur <note>original: Sulphur</note> / and [call it] by many other names / <margin>X</margin> and this work is made from the dry and the moist / the first composition / out of which the body <note>original: Corpus</note> of Magnesia is made. Rasis says: Take our lead or our Magnesia; the body of Magnesia is a body that dissolves <note>original: Soluirt</note> / so that one may compose the spirit <note>original: Spiritum</note> into it / another philosopher <note>original: Philosophus</note> says / I tell you / that nature is a man and a woman / and they have called it Magnesia because there is a great secret within it.

Quicksilver <note>original: Argentum viuum</note> is a spirit / which is retained with the body / or the body of Magnesia is a body / which they dissolve / so that they may compose the spirit into it / Magnesia is a body and a spirit / therefore when the philosophers speak / of our lead / our gold <note>original: ☉; the astrological symbol for the Sun, representing gold in alchemy</note> / our Magnesia / understand that as our ore / sulfur is the ore / and the ore is the entire perfection of the first composition / and the first composition from the dry / which is called the body of magnesia / and is also the composition of the 4 bodies / of the 4 elements / these 4 bodies / are called sulfur of the earth <note>original: sulphur terrae</note> / says Plato. The sulfur is the soul <note>original: Anima</note> / which is hidden in the 4 bodies / and the tinting soul <note>original: tingierende anima; the transformative essence that gives the Stone its power to change the color and nature of metals</note> is correct / which [comes] out of the 4 bodies / that is / out of the 4 elements / and out of these 4 bodies of the elements / in this our composition of the <margin>X</margin> body of Magnesia / you must take equal parts of them / says Socrates. The ore and the lead / become a beautiful stone / mix them equally / and cook gold <note>original: aurum</note> with it.

## Chapter seven:

<margin>X</margin> The perfect mixing occurs through cooking, grinding, and washing. A philosopher says: through good governance <term>Regiment: the controlled management of heat and timing in the alchemical process</term> the thick body is made thin, and its impurity is burned away and washed off; and its fiery subtlety, which is hidden in its belly—which is its tincture <note>original: Tinctur; the transformative essence or color-changing power</note> and soul <note>original: anima</note>—is elevated and hidden within the other spirit. Morienes <note>Morienus, a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist</note> says: You must mix the thick with the fiery poisons, and you must putrefy <note>original: putrificieren; to rot or break down through heat and moisture</note> them and grind them diligently, so that one spirit is hidden with the other spirit. Plato <note>The ancient Greek philosopher, who was often cited as an alchemical authority in medieval and Renaissance texts</note> says: Spirits separated from the body and hidden in another spirit have both become volatile. Eximenes <note>Likely Anaximenes, another philosopher-figure from the alchemical tradition</note> says: Unless you grind them diligently with the fire, it will not otherwise rise up.

And therefore there is a common proverb: if you can give fire to Mercury <note>original: Mercurio; represented by the symbol ☿</note>, it is sufficient. The fire that burns the Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> burns the bodies and makes them subtle, and separates the coarse from the subtle; therefore it is called a fire. Menaldus says: Know that quicksilver <note>original: argentum viuum</note> is a fire that burns, mortifies <note>original: mortificiert; "kills" or fundamentally alters the state of a substance</note>, and breaks the bodies apart through a [steady] governance.

# Concerning the Stone
<note>original: De lapide</note>

...living [spirit] <note>original: viuum; continuing from the previous page's word "spirit"</note>, in the mixture it is called a fiery poison <note>original: Venenum; in alchemy, this refers to a corrosive or transformative agent that breaks down substances to their primal state</note>. Through the fire it is prepared, through the body of Magnesia <note>original: Corpus Magnesiæ</note>, and through the corpses of men <note>original: Leichnam der Menschen; an allegorical term for the solid, "dead" metallic remains or the dark sediment at the bottom of a flask</note>. The fiery poison is the useful water; therefore, observe and experience it diligently. The so-called governance <term>Regiment: the controlled management of heat and timing in the alchemical process</term> ensures that the body <note>original: Corpus</note> is sublimated into the aforementioned spirit <note>original: Spiritum</note>, and likewise dissolved <note>original: soluirt</note>, so that it becomes tangible; and the spirit coagulates <note>original: coagulirt; thickens or solidifies</note> in the body like milk, and both together are light and intangible like butter.

Plato: when the spirit is separated from the body and is hidden within the other spirit, then they both become volatile. The Philosopher Mundus <note>A character from the 'Turba Philosophorum,' one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts</note>: unless you make the things thin, so that they rise up like a spirit, it is all for nothing. This art is nothing other than thirst and water; when the bodies <note>original: Corpora</note> are ground diligently and when they are raised up, they become more fixed <note>original: Fixer; the quality of being resistant to fire and not evaporating</note>.

<margin>X</margin>
Therefore, when the bodies become liquid, ground, and elevated, a tincture <term>Tincture: the transformative essence or "dye" of the Stone that changes the nature of other metals</term> of our ore is produced from them. This is called quicksilver <note>original: Argentum viuum; literally "living silver"</note> in our art. Therefore, our stone is now earth, and our earth is fire, our fire is air, our air is water, our water is spirit, our spirit is soul, the soul is a corpse, and the corpse is the earth. And in the fire are the two elements, in the water is air—the two elements. These are the four bodies of the elements of which I have spoken.

For all the philosophers have said: whatever is hot is their fire, and whatever is volatile is their water, and whatever rises upward is their air, and whatever coagulates is their stone and earth. Here it should be noted that the Sun <note>original: ☉ (Sol); representing gold and the active, fiery principle</note> is their fire and Mercury <note>original: ☿; representing quicksilver and the principle of air/volatility</note> is their air, and the dissolution <note>original: Solution</note> is their water, and in the coagulation <note>original: Coagulation</note> is the earth and the stone.

Hermes Trismegistus the Philosopher <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the father of alchemy</note>: his power is whole,

...when it is turned into a black earth—that is, from moisture to dryness, and towards stability—which turns all imperfect bodies into perfect gold <note>original: ☉; the symbol for Sol or Gold</note> and silver <note>original: ☾; the symbol for Luna or Silver</note>. And take note: when you have the smoke within the body <note>original: Corpore</note>, you should leave the medicine in the fire for another 15 or 21 days, so that the invisible spirits may unite well and remain within the matter, becoming a water and a perfected matter, leading to the perfect, true redness <term>Rubedo: the final "red" stage of the alchemical work, signifying completion and the highest power of the Stone</term>. Also know that in this sublimation, the four elements are truly separated, as the philosophers say; for our work and our stone are nothing other than the separation of the elements. For in our stone, two elements are visible—water and earth—and the other two are hidden—air and fire. Therefore, when the philosophers see the matter ascending in the smoke, they call it the "ascension"; and this sublimation must occur with a gentle fire, so that the transforming <term>Tingierende: from "tingere," meaning the power to "dye" or transmute the nature of a base metal into a noble one</term> soul rises into the heights of the water, and the coarseness remains behind on the bottom.

Menaldus <note>A philosopher frequently cited in the "Turba Philosophorum," one of the earliest Latin alchemical texts</note>: the thick and impure does not transform; only the subtle does. Emidius the Philosopher: from which a pure spirit <note>original: Spiritus</note> rises with a gentle fire, and every pure flower <note>alchemical term for the finest, most volatile part of a substance</note> is sublimated; and that which is sublimated is the quicksilver of the chamber <note>original: Argentum viuum cambræ</note>, which remains as Water and Gum-Vinegar <note>original: Gummi Essig; likely referring to a corrosive, resinous solvent used to dissolve metals</note>. It is the One that transforms our ore and has many other names. In the sublimation of the work lies its perfection; when the earth, which was so black, has become white—this is the noblest good. It is then called the "white flying earth," <margin>X</margin> the white sulfur, or the magnesia. This white earth is now prepared to receive its origin and soul. Upon this, Plato says: sow your gold <note>original: ☉</note> and silver <note>original: ☾</note> into the white earth (which is now prepared to receive), and it will bring forth a thousand-fold fruit.

## Chapter Eight.

The second work of our art is that our ore <term>Ertz: the raw mineral or metallic starting material for the alchemical process</term> be transformed with our water <note>original: Aqua</note> into a tincturing venom <term>Tingierend Venenum: a potent, transformative substance (often called 'poison' or 'venom') that has the power to 'bite' into and penetrate base metals to change their nature</term> or redness. This comes from the second work, which arises from gold <note>original: ☉, the symbol for the Sun or Gold</note> alone; for the governance of our ore is that it becomes a tincturing venom. And all the ancients have said: whoever can bring gold into a tincturing venom has arrived at the true truth, and whoever cannot do so labors in vain.

<margin>X // '' ''</margin>
Therefore all the philosophers say: our stone is joined together with three things—with the body of the origin, which is the soul wherein the fluid life is buried; through the living water, which is called the spirit; and then our ore is tinctured and brought, unchanged, into a tincturing venom through the permanent water <note>original: bleibend Wasser; a solvent that does not evaporate in the fire</note>, or through quicksilver of the chamber <note>original: Argentum viuum cambræ</note>, or water of sulfur <note>original: Aquam sulphuris</note>, or the like.

And although these are many names, there is nonetheless no more than one water, composed from our things and completed through its governance, which governance is hidden by the will of God from all the ignorant. Parmenides the philosopher says: gold is not transformed into a venomous lead and ore unless it is moistened with the vinegar <note>original: Aceto</note> well known to the wise philosophers. Rosinus the philosopher: when you work with gold in the art of sulfur water, you can make pure gold from it, and that is a perfection <term>Perfection: the final, stable state of the alchemical matter</term>. Our ore is tinctured through the worthiness of the fire, for the long cooking of the fire warms its tincture within it.

Hermes the philosopher: our son the King <note>An allegorical figure for the emerging Stone or the perfected gold</note> receives his tincture from the fire. From all this it is concluded that the composition of the tincturing elixir is from our ore and our permanent water, which is led through the governance of the fire to such tincturing power; and he who can govern the composition of our permanent water...

# Of the Philosophers.

...[we] must mix our ore with our water; you should beat our ore into thin plates <note>original: lamminas</note> and mix them with the water, and put them in a gentle fire so that they dissolve <note>original: Soluieren</note> and become one thing.

Aristotle the Philosopher says: the body <note>original: Corpus</note> that I have made known to you, <margin>X</margin> beat it thin; thereafter put it into our permanent water and regulate it with a gentle fire, so that the plates break and become water; Theophilus and Balcus the Philosopher say the same: take our iron and beat it into thin plates, then mix it with the venom <note>original: Veneno; in alchemy, "venom" or "poison" often refers to a potent, transformative solvent or the raw, "unrefined" state of the mercury</note>. Arles the Philosopher says: after that, they placed me and my companions into a shining skin <note>likely referring to a glass vessel or a specific film that forms during the process</note> and led us into hell <note>a metaphor for the intense heat of the furnace</note>.

Rosinus the Philosopher says: when you have mixed them, then <margin>X</margin> put them into the house of transparency—or the transparent poverty—and in this governance, many colors will appear: first black, then white, then yellow, and finally it will come to the perfect redness <note>original: rötigkeit</note>, as you will hear hereafter. Diomedes the Philosopher says: cook them so that they become black, thereafter white, thereafter red; then they will become a tincturing venom <note>original: Tingirendes Venenum; a substance capable of "tinging" or transforming other metals</note>. Geber the Philosopher says: unless our work is first made white, we cannot otherwise have nor make the Red <note>original: Rubeum; the final stage of the Great Work</note>.

Eximines the Philosopher says: unless you make our ore white and thereafter red, all else is in vain. Parmenides says: make gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> into pennies, and pennies again into gold. Siodorus the Philosopher says: the beginning of the entire work is the white color, thereafter comes the red; then it is well-made. This composition <margin>X</margin> you shall cook in a small fire in its vessel for 40 days or 42. Aristotle says: put them in a small fire so that the tablets break and become water. Mundus the Philosopher says: mix the portions and cook them for 40 days.

Thelus the Philosopher says: cook it in its water for 42 days, and in this cooking, before the white color, the black color appears, which is of the nature of Mars <note>original symbol: ♂; often associated with iron or the quality of "hardness" being broken down</note>. ## Chapter Twelve.

Therefore, the power and virtue of the Elixir is such that through the properties it has received from Nature and from Art, it is powerful enough to cast away all impurity and to tinge all imperfect bodies <note>original: *Imperfecta Corpora*; these are "base" metals like lead, tin, or iron, which alchemists believed were simply gold that had been corrupted or "stunted" in the earth.</note> into true gold. It is also powerful enough to make a human healthy and to bring them into a balanced state of quality. This is a gift of God and a secret of the ancient philosophers and sages, which kings and princes could not obtain unless God granted it; and no one can rightly understand the sayings of philosophy unless he has it from God or from a Master.

Therefore all philosophers say that this work of the noble and divine art is very often and deeply hidden. For they recognized the great power, strength, and virtue within it, and from their great wisdom they learned and took what this Art gives. Through it, they also possessed the health of their lives and took for their bodies all strength and joy from this divine Art and its secrets. Therefore, whoever truly understands this, my First Book, is a Son of Wisdom and shall thank God manifoldly that He has revealed such an inexpressible treasure to him. But whoever does not understand this book should not blame the sages, but rather himself, for the sake of his own ignorance.

### Concerning the Yellow [One]

[He] speaks with more pleasant words and will ask you: "My dear, what do you seek here? For truly, I have not seen any person here for a long time, so near to this house." Then you shall answer him: "I have been directed here and I seek the **Stone of the Philosophers**" <note>original: *Lapidem Philosophorum*; the legendary substance believed to transmute base metals into gold and grant eternal life.</note>. You shall go into the house until you come to a flowing spring; follow it until you come to the source. There you will find a small vein of the spring’s pure water, the **Virgin's Milk** <note>A term often used by alchemists to describe a white, corrosive liquid or a specific stage of mercurial purification.</note>. You shall answer him: 'I seek the **Stone of the Philosophers**.' Then he will ask you: 'Who directed you here?' Answer him: 'A **Yellow Man**.' Then the **Red Man** will also ask you: 'Have you found the **Virgin's Milk**?' Answer: 'Yes, I have a glass full.' 'Since you have the **milk**, I will also direct you further.'"

You must consider how you will take it from him. Now, you cannot take it from him with kindness, for he is wicked and does not willingly release it; for he knows well that when the **White Dove** leaves him, he must die instantly. Therefore, he holds it fast."

# On Geber
<note>Geber refers to Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–815), a foundational figure in alchemy whose writings emphasize the balance of the four qualities—hot, cold, wet, and dry—and the mercury-sulfur theory of metals.</note>

There are also in our Stone <term>Stone: the Philosopher's Stone, the goal of the alchemical work</term> only two tangible and visible elements that keep the other two hidden, being neither seen nor grasped. Earth and Water are visible, but the Air within the Water is invisible to us, and the Fire within the Earth is also invisible, being neither seen nor grasped. No one perceives the virtue <note>virtue: in this context, the inherent power or spiritual essence of the material</note> except within the primary two elements, Earth and Water, and through the action of Fire it is transformed into a true Whiteness and Redness <note>Whiteness and Redness: the *Albedo* and *Rubedo*, stages signaling the purification and final perfection of the alchemical matter</note>.

Take heed of the grace of God; here is the second element in our Stone, which is the blackness and the **Raven’s Head** <term>Raven’s Head: *caput corvi*, the symbolic name for the *nigredo* or black stage, representing the death and decomposition of the substance necessary before rebirth</term>—a mother, a hatchling, a root, which all other things follow and upon which they are planted, as in a mother or the soil. It is called by many strange names by the natural Masters, such as *latan* <note>original: *latan*, likely referring to *laton*, a term for an impure metallic body or "black lead" that must be cleansed</note>, a treasure, a black sheaf, yeast, our metal, our mother, our death (which also devours husband and wife), and many other names that all mean one thing, which comes from one thing. Therefore, through such sublimation <term>sublimation: the process of purifying a substance by heating it to a gas and back to a solid</term>, it is converted, attained, and brought about; and the fleeting becomes stable, the soft becomes hard, and the watery becomes earthy. 

And then Geber says: the transformation occurs from one nature into the other, as cold compares itself with heat, and dry—or a spirit—to a body <note>original: *Spiritus zu Corpus*</note>, or thin to thick, or from a hidden thing to a manifest thing; and likewise, a manifest thing to a hidden thing. As the Masters speak in many ways, they say the action of our Stone is nothing other than the transformation of nature and a union <note>original: *eringnus*, likely *Einigung* (uniting)</note> of the elements; for thus moisture turns to dryness, the flowing into the stable, spirit to body, thin to thick, watery into fiery, and air into earth, whereby the elements are transformed one into the other. And thus you have the first chapter of this matter.

# Of the Rebis, a Stone.

<image-desc>A large historiated woodcut initial 'D' containing a human face amidst scrolling foliate ornamentation.</image-desc>
You should know that in this Art there are three kinds of Stones which, by God's grace, work wonderful things. Aristotle <note>Medieval alchemists frequently attributed their findings to Aristotle to lend them authority, though these were usually pseudo-Aristotelian texts</note> wrote of these in his books, in which all power lies according to this Art. From it, one makes a powder that the Masters call an <term>Elixir</term> <note>A substance believed to be capable of changing base metals into gold or silver, or acting as a universal cure</note>, which transforms all impure bodies <note>original: "Corpus"; refers to base metals like lead or tin</note> into **Gold** <term>☉</term> and **Silver** <term>☽</term> that is better than the natural **Gold** and **Silver**. I will, however, write of no more than one, called the <term>Rebis</term> <note>From the Latin *res-bis*, meaning "double-thing." It represents the "hermaphroditic" union of opposites, such as spirit and matter or sulfur and mercury</note>; for you will find it in all places. It is the <term>Fifth Essence</term> <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; the purest substance in nature, beyond the four elements</note>, described here in few words. Take it fresh with its blood and cut it to the width of a fingernail; if it were not of a joyful nature, it would not mix with **Mercury** <term>☿</term>. But because they are of one nature, they mix together so that the fire cannot harm it. Take one pound of it and put it into four pounds of **Alkali Salt** <term>Salalcali</term> water, and take a child’s urine <note>In early chemistry, urine was a common source of ammonia and phosphorus</note>, and put it all into a glazed pot with a narrow neck. Boil it with a gentle fire until it is half boiled away, so that you can see it through the hole at the top. Guard yourself against the steam or the smell, otherwise it kills! <note>A warning against toxic fumes, likely mercury vapors or ammonia</note> And when the water is half boiled away, you will find the **Rebis** transformed into water. As the volatile substances are produced, let it cool and strain it through a cloth, and throw the **dregs** <note>original: "Fæces"; the solid waste or residue remaining after distillation or straining</note> away. This is the Stone that the Masters write about; it is a stone and yet is no stone. You find it in all places: on the plains, on the mountains, in the depths, and in all waters. Both the rich and the poor possess it. It is the most wretched of all things, and yet the most precious of all things <note>This is a classic alchemical riddle describing the *Prima Materia*, the base material needed for the Great Work, which is often hidden in plain sight or considered worthless by the ignorant</note>. Purify the water seven times, as you know, and what

Put it into the little pot and act in every way as you did above with the White work. Thus you will have noble **Gold** <term>☉</term>, and that is the **Elixir**; in one hour, it transforms all purified **bodies** <note>original: *Corpora*; referring to base metals</note> into good **Gold** <term>☉</term>, **Tin** <term>♃</term>, and **Lead** <term>♄</term>.

...secret of all arts of the whole world / a heavenly unpurchasable treasure of all treasures / as Plato says: He who has this great gift of God / has the mastery of the world / for he has come to the end / and has obtained the wealth / and breaks the bonds of Nature / not for himself alone / for he has the power to transform all imperfect metallic bodies / into the most perfect and purest **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> as can ever be.

### AVICENNA'S SEVEN <note>original: "AVICENNAE SEPTEM REGULÆ"</note>
#### rules, from which the Philosopher's

#### 1. Rule.

The first operation is that the noblest substance, which

#### 2. Rule.

The matter or <term>subject</term> <note>original: "subiectum"; the base material undergoing transformation.</note> should be dissolved into water.

#### 3. Rule.

<term>Putrefaction</term> <note>original: "feulung"; a stage of decay necessary for rebirth.</note> must precede generation, for the

birth of the other.

coarse matter be washed and purified from all
corrupting impurities. However, the philosophers say:
the longer the water remains over the earth, the more it is
washed clean.

#### 5. Rule.

Next follows <term>coagulation</term> <note>The process of a liquid thickening or becoming solid.</note>, for our water must,
through the gentle heat and cooking of our sun, be
dried into earth and become a powder.

## 6. Rule.

After that, it must be <term>calcined</term> <note>original: "Calciniert"; the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder or "ash."</note>. # ON THE QUINTESSENCE
## Of Wine.

<image-desc>A large woodcut decorative initial letter Z, filled with ornate floral scrolls and leaf patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

To begin, take in the name of God clear Rhine wine, or another beautiful clear wine that has been drawn off the lees <note>original: "von der Mutter sey gezogen"; literally "drawn from the mother," referring to the sediment or dregs at the bottom of the cask.</note>, for there must be no turbidity within it. For the philosophers <note>A term for early scientists and alchemists.</note> say that one must extract our Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and providing an elixir of life.</note> from one single thing, without adding any foreign matter. Therefore, take beautiful clear wine that is good in scent and taste; from this, separate its four elements <term>Elements: In ancient and medieval science, these are Fire, Air, Water, and Earth, which were believed to make up all matter.</term> as much as is possible to do. 

For to separate the elements perfectly—namely, to draw out the Air from the Fire at the same time—that is impossible, for Air is hot and moist. Thus, one cannot perfectly separate the moisture from the heat. Likewise, Water is cold and moist, so one cannot perfectly separate the cold from the moisture. Furthermore, Fire is hot and dry, so one cannot separate the heat from the dryness. Therefore, it is impossible to separate the elements cleanly from one another; instead, they must remain mixed together, for in every element there are two natures: one is manifest <note>Visible or obvious to the senses.</note> and the other is secret <note>Hidden or internal.</note>.

Example <note>original: "Exemplum"</note>: Water is cold and moist; the moisture is manifest, but the cold is secret and invisible, and is a soul without a body, hidden beneath the moisture. Air is hot and moist; the moisture is manifest,

...and visible; Heat, however, is a spirit, and secret. Fire is hot and dry, and clear, and is both subtle <term>Subtle: In alchemy, this describes a substance that is refined, thin, or volatile, like a gas or vapor.</term> and spiritual <term>Spiritual: Here, this refers to the "spirit" or volatile essence of a substance that can be captured through distillation, rather than a religious meaning.</term>.

Its clarity and redness are manifest <note>Visible or obvious to the senses.</note>, but its heat is hidden as dryness. For when you see a light burning, you will clearly see the clarity and redness with your eyes from the outside; but the heat that the fire contains within itself you cannot see. However, if you thrust a finger into the light, you will certainly feel or perceive the invisible heat. Earth is cold and dry; its dry body is visible and tangible, but its coldness is invisible, and a spirit without a body.

Thus it is manifest that it is impossible to separate the elements from one another, for they must be mixed with one another. Nevertheless, we should do so as much as is possible for us to do. We may separate them, as we shall teach hereafter, and rectify <note>original: "vertificieren"; likely a variation of "rectificieren," meaning to purify a substance through repeated distillation.</note> them of their imperfection. We can make them pure, beautiful, hard, and fixed <term>Fixed: A "fix" or "fixed" substance is one that has been rendered stable and no longer evaporates or is destroyed when exposed to high heat.</term> when they are united, so that they may never again be separated from one another. It shall be a clarified body <note>original: "clarificiert Corpus"</note> for eternity, which cannot be consumed by fire.

Aristotle says in a small book that he made: everything that is in the earth is of two natures. One is secret, the other is manifest. That which by nature shines from the outside has its opposite within. That which is hot and dry on the outside is moist and cold on the inside. Therefore, let us now see how we shall overturn all things and set their interior to the outside, and vice versa <note>original: "è conuerso"</note>. Thus we may create a perfect work, and this must happen from one single thing, without adding any foreign matter to it.

# Of the fifth [essence]

# Concerning the Fifth [Essence]

For without the **Earth**, no thing can be perfect; for the **Earth** is firm and the foundation <note>literally: "firmament"</note> of all perfection; and without the **Earth**, no thing can be **fixed** <note>In alchemy, to "fix" a substance is to make a volatile spirit stable and resistant to heat.</note>, nor can any thing gain the power of strength, except from the **Earth**. And you should know that the **Earth** is very small in quantity, but possesses great powers.

One sees from a single small grain many grains spring forth; then see well to it that you do not take foreign things, but rather the substance's own **Earth**. For there are some who intend to make the **water of life** <note>original: *aquam vitæ*, a term for concentrated alcohol or a restorative elixir</note> and instead make the **water of death** <note>original: *aquam mortis*</note>. This is the reason: they take foreign Earth and say that such is the substance's own **Earth**. Others say the wine from the press or vat with the grapes and **seeds** <note>original: *Steinlein*</note>, and claim it is a perfect **Earth**. Others take grapevines, burn them to ashes, and make a **lye** <note>An alkaline solution produced by leaching wood ashes.</note> from them, which they **coagulate** <note>To thicken or solidify a liquid into a solid mass.</note> and say it is the **earth of wine** <note>original: *terra vini*</note>. However, they all err together, and while they intend to make **waters of life**, they become **waters of death**. But the **Philosophers** <note>original: *Philosophici*; referring to alchemical authorities</note> say: you shall make that which is perfect from one thing alone, and add nothing foreign to it. If you use grapes from the press that are not yet perfect for human necessity, and you wish to extract the **Elements** from them as previously taught, the **Earth** that remains afterward is its own **Earth**, and not foreign.

**Example**: when the wine comes out of the press, it is foul and unclear, and it bubbles up every spring; its **dregs** <note>original: *Faeces*</note> and yeast sit at the bottom. It also separates from itself the **tartar** <note>original: *Weinstein*, the potassium bitartrate crystals that form in wine barrels.</note> on the sides of the barrel, which are also nothing but **dregs**. Thus the wine pushes away all **dregs** and all evil **humors** <note>original: *Humores*, the fluids or temperaments of a substance.</note> from itself—above, and below on the bottom, and on all sides. When it becomes clear and beautiful, having cast off all its **dregs**, it also gains a good smell and taste and is very lovely to drink and to take into the body; and only then is it a single, unified thing.

But as long as it has any **dregs** or turbidity about it...

### Of the Fifth [Essence] <note>original: *De quinta*</note> ###

The natural moisture of the nature of the human <term>body</term> <note>original: *corporis*</note> is consumed and brought to nothing; for the life of all humans and animals depends upon two things: that is, upon heat and moisture. Therefore, in no medicinal work should you take the element of Fire. <term>Air</term> <note>original: *Lufft*</note> is hot and moist, <term>Earth</term> <note>original: *Erden*</note> is cool and dry; and with the coldness of the Earth, you shall temper the heat of the Air. In this way, you may properly make a <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: *Quinta essentia*; the "fifth essence," a purified spirit beyond the four elements</note> or a clarified **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> and the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: *Lapidem Philosophorum*</note>. ->The Essence of Wine<- <note>original: *essentia vini*</note>

Put it in a water bath <note>original: *B.*, abbreviation for *Balneum Mariae*</note> with the glass well-sealed on top, and let it stand there for 4 or 5 days. Then take it out and place it on a furnace in ashes; seal the <term>alembic</term> <note>original: *Helm* (helm or cap); the top part of a still</note> with <term>lute</term> <note>original: *lutier*; a paste used to make joints airtight</note>, and place a receiver <note>original: *Recipienten*</note> in front of it. **Distil** first with gentle fire, then gradually stronger, **continuing** in this way until no more distils over. Then let it cool; your "Earth" should remain lying at the bottom of the vessel. Take it out, grind it on a stone with a "wine" made of your **rectified** water <note>the highly purified spirit previously distilled</note>; grind it so fine and **refined** <note>original: *Subtil*</note> that one could paint with it using a brush. Then put your ground Earth back into the glass and pour the "Air" <note>the distilled spirit/liquid</note> back onto it, stir it well together, and put it back in the water bath, well-sealed, for 4 or 5 days. Stir it well once every day so that it mixes thoroughly. Then take it out, set it back in the ashes, and **distil** it over again through the alembic <note>original: *per Alembicum*</note> as was previously described.

Repeat such **distillation** so often until the Earth has completely **distilled** itself over. And note, there is yet another way to distil the Earth that is easier. Once the Earth has come over, it is as the **Physician** <note>original: *Phisicus*; likely referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary author of the Emerald Tablet</note> says: "The lowest must be as the highest," or else no **conjunction** or joining together can occur, for the Earth must be made spiritual <note>transformed from a solid into a volatile vapor</note>.

Therefore, all the wise say: "Make the lowest as the highest, and the highest as the lowest," and so you will have a well-made, firm work. And if the Earth were made volatile and the Air made **fixed** <note>original: *Fix*; stable and resistant to heat</note>, and the Earth did not go over with the Air, they could never unite or **be fixed** <note>original: *Figieren*</note>. For when they distil over together, they take hold of one another at the bottom, and such a union occurs there that they may never again be separated. It shall remain an eternal **conjunction**, just as it will be with our body and soul after the Last Judgment; for then there shall be no "mixedness" of the **elements**, but they shall become a **simple** being <note>original: *Simbel Wesen*; a pure, indivisible essence</note>, a single-natured thing.

### On the Fifth [Essence]

...you must make your fire stronger until you see that no more veins or streaks move up and down in the glass. Then you shall keep the material <note>original: *Materia*</note> in such heat for eight days; then you will see another sign that the philosophers <note>Alchemists often referred to themselves simply as "philosophers" or "lovers of wisdom."</note> write of so wonderfully, and it is a sign of perfection.

For Aristotle speaks in the fifteenth chapter of the *Secret of Secrets* <note>original: *de secretis Secretorum*; a widely read medieval book of advice and occult lore attributed to Aristotle, though likely written by a later author</note>: our water is not water, nor a pouring of water; it is our instrument, and our hammer, axe, file, or plane with which we must work. Just as a blacksmith must forge the iron with the hammer if he is to bring it to his will, and once the iron is beaten according to the master’s will with the hammer, he hangs the tool on the wall; or as the carpenter works with the axe, but once the work is finished, the axe does not remain with the work, but rather he hangs it on the wall.

So it is now even more so with our work. For the "water of the clouds" <note>likely referring to distilled water or the volatile spirit that has been purified</note> is the hammer or axe with which we must make and complete our work. For with the water of the clouds, we must unbind or dissolve <note>original: *soluiren*; to break a substance down into its component parts</note> all our work; also with it, we must draw out and separate the elements. And when we have separated them, we must wash them with water—just as a woman washes her linen in water. And when it is already washed, she hangs it in the sun; then she no longer needs the washing. And look at the cloth-dyers: when they want to dye cloth or garments, they cannot bring the color into the cloth without the "water of the clouds." They must prepare the color with the water and boil the color with the fire, without the cloth. Then, once the cloth is dyed, they hang it up to dry; the water dries out, and the color remains fixed <note>original: *Fix*; in alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that has become stable and can no longer be evaporated or changed by fire</note> in the cloth.

# Concerning the Fifth <note>original: "De quinta"; likely referring to the *Quinta Essentia* or Fifth Essence.</note>

Therefore, first let the glass become quite cold before you remove the water from it; for the water ensures that the stone does not penetrate through. For as long as the glass is pure, the stone is melted; for it dissolves in the hot dryness, and in the cold, moist air it coagulates. Therefore, let it become quite cold.

When the water is gone, break the glass and take out the "King of Eternity," which crown and power he shall always keep; and thank Almighty God for His holy gifts, etc.

Now is fulfilled what was praised before: our stone shall be made, say the *Natural Philosophers* <note>original: "Physici"; in this context, the term refers to practitioners of natural philosophy or alchemy.</note> from one thing, without adding anything foreign. And it shall have within it the four elements, which is then sufficiently taught and proven by understanding and discourse. Therefore says *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of alchemy.</note>: You shall not open your purse to incur great costs. And *Arnaldus de Villa Nova* <note>A famous 13th-century physician and alchemist.</note> says in his *New Testament* <note>original: "Nouo Testamento"; referring to a specific alchemical treatise by Arnaldus.</note>: God the Lord has given us two stones, one for the White and one for the Red, which we may have for free where they grow; and one may have them as much as one wants, and one need not ask anyone for permission. And he who knows this stone and can prepare it as understood, he needs no longer incur great expense with the <term>Art<note>The 'Art' refers to the study and practice of alchemy.</note></term>.

Therefore, keep well in your memory what I have shown you here; I have opened the door for you. So go now joyfully into the house of *Philosophy* <note>In the early modern period, "Philosophy" often referred to Natural Philosophy, of which alchemy was a branch.</note>, and set to work with your modest understanding; so shall you see and understand wonderful things. For I have told and written everything clearly to you, without any hidden words, and have opened the path for you which I have walked with great care and labor, and have relieved you of your care and labor. ## The Emerald [Table] of Hermes Trisme-
## gistus, father of philosophers. <note>original: "Schmaragdina Hermetis Trismegisti patris philosophorum."</note>

Following hereafter is the Emerald Tablet, which Hermes Trismegistus made, and which was found after his death in a cave where he lay buried, held within his very hands. This Hermes lived after the <term>Great Flood<note>German: "Sundtfluß"; refers to the biblical Deluge of Noah. This Hermes is the first who, after the Flood, created and described the <term>Philosopher’s Stone<note>The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life; the ultimate goal of the "Work."</note></term>; for this reason, he is called a Father of all Sages.

<meta>This page continues the instructional poem from the previous page, further discussing the nature of the "One Matter" and the cryptic names given to it by ancient authorities. It emphasizes that while the substance is common and easily found, the secrets of its composition and the regulation of fire are the most difficult steps to master.</meta>

### 247.

->Zu<-

Although there is but one **Matter**,
Which is in no way otherwise refined,
Than that it be <term>clarified</term> <note>original: "clarificirt," meaning to purify a substance until it is clear or transparent, often through distillation or sublimation.</note>;
Yet its name has misled many.
Still, I have revealed enough to you
In many various ways, forms, and manners.
Therefore, the names are many, I say;
Do not let them lead you away from the path.
The ancients write in their scriptures:
It is a <term>Dragon</term> <note>original: "Track," a common alchemical symbol for the raw, volatile, or "mercurial" starting material.</note>, a great poison.
Another calls it a monstrous serpent;
It is said to be everywhere and not expensive:
All people possess it at once,
In all the world, both poor and rich.
It is the property of the metals,
Through which it victoriously overcomes.
It is a **Perfection** of the same,
And places a golden crown upon it.
Now the practitioner completes [the work],
He who understands it and knows the **matter**:
Only two things have been left out,
Which, however, you shall certainly find,
If you follow the right path,
And care diligently for your work.
The **composition** <note>original: "zsamensetzung," likely referring to the *Coniunctio* or the joining of the "male" and "female" principles in the flask.</note> is the one,
Which the wise have kept secret;
The nature of the **fire** also has a secret cunning,
Therefore its regulation is the other [secret]:
So that one does not do too much to it,
Otherwise the whole game is lost.

<summary>The author explains that the "One Matter" of alchemy is hidden behind many symbolic names like "Dragon" or "Poison" and is a common substance available to everyone. He identifies the two greatest secrets as the correct mixing of ingredients and the precise control of the fire's heat.</summary>
<keywords>Prima Materia, Dragon, Poison, Serpent, Perfection, Practitioner, Composition, Fire, Alchemical Names</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the alchemical instructional poem begun on the previous page. It moves from the technical aspects of fire regulation to the moral and spiritual requirements of the practitioner, ending with the publication details of the volume.</meta>

One cannot treat it too gently,
Just as the hen hatches the chick:
Thus it shall be in the beginning,
Time itself provides the evidence:
For as the **fire** is applied,
Accordingly this **Treasure** <term>Treasure</term> <note>original: "Schatz," a common metaphor for the Philosopher's Stone or the successful completion of the Great Work.</note> is brought forth:
Be diligent, steadfast, peaceful, and pious,
Pray that God also comes to your aid:
If you attain this, then see to it,
That the poor are always recommended to your care. <note>It was a standard alchemical trope that the "Stone" was a gift from God, and the recipient was bound by a moral oath to use the resulting wealth for charitable works and the relief of the poor.</note>
